domain: Contractors State License Law (B&P Code Division 3, Chapter 9), Articles 6-8.5: CSLB arbitration (B&P 7085(b)-7085.9), Solar Energy System Restitution Program (7086-7086.11, repealed), disciplinary proceedings incl. citations, civil penalties, letters of admonishment, records, prompt payment, grounds for discipline and public disclosure (7090-7124.6), workers' compensation insurance reports and stop orders (7125-7127), revenue and fee schedule (7135-7138.1), and the Construction Management Education Sponsorship Act (7139-7139.5)
source_doc: 2026 CSLB California Contractors License Law & Reference Book (official), Section VI, book Chapter 8 (Business and Professions Code), PDF pages 325-381 (B&P 7085(b) through 7139.5); file chunk lawbook_p326-380.txt

rules.title: Small-dollar complaints must go to CSLB arbitration
rules.plain_english: If a complaint alleges a possible violation of the sections listed in B&P 7085(a)(1) and the contract price or the damages demanded is at or below the contractor bond amount required by B&P 7071.6, CSLB must refer the complaint to its arbitration program (mandatory arbitration).

parameters.trigger: possible violation of the sections listed in B&P 7085(a)(1)
parameters.threshold_test: contract price OR demand for damages <= bond amount required under B&P 7071.6
parameters.result: complaint shall be referred to arbitration
parameters.bond_amount_source: B&P 7071.6(a): contractor's bond "in the sum of twenty-five thousand dollars ($25,000)" (2026 CSLB Law Book, PDF page 295)

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors and complainants (owners) in CSLB complaints
rules.verbatim_quote: In all cases in which a possible violation of the sections set forth in paragraph (1) of subdivision (a) exists and the contract price, or the demand for damages is equal to or less than the amount of the bond required under Section 7071.6, but, regardless of the contract price, the complaint shall be referred to arbitration
rules.notes: The 7071.6 bond is $25,000 (PDF page 295), so mandatory referral applies at or below $25,000. The sections in 7085(a)(1) are 7107, 7109, 7110, 7113, 7119 and 7120 (PDF page 324). For voluntary arbitration under 7085(a), "material damages" means more than the 7071.6(a) bond amount but less than $50,000. The printed sentence is ambiguous ("but, regardless of the contract price"); read with the full statute.

verification.checked_against: 2026 CSLB Law Book (sources/lawbook.txt), PDF pages 324-325 (B&P 7085(a)-(b)); PDF page 295 (B&P 7071.6(a) bond amount)
verification.correction: No error. Added bond_amount_usd = 25000 from B&P 7071.6(a) (PDF page 295) and the 7085(a)(1) section list (PDF page 324) so the threshold can be computed; the original note said the amount was not on these pages.

rules.title: Arbitrator's award is a CSLB registrar order
rules.plain_english: An award issued by a CSLB arbitrator counts as an order of the Registrar, so ignoring it has licensing consequences (see automatic suspension under B&P 7085.6).
rules.applies_to: Licensees and complainants in CSLB arbitration
rules.verbatim_quote: An arbitrator may render an award and that award shall be deemed to be an order of the registrar.

rules.title: Return voluntary agreement to arbitrate within 30 calendar days
rules.plain_english: When CSLB decides a dispute is suitable for voluntary arbitration under B&P 7085(a), it mails an agreement to arbitrate to both the owner and the contractor. It must be returned within 30 calendar days of the mailing date; returning it authorizes CSLB to proceed. CSLB must also explain the consequences of choosing arbitration over court and that parties may hire counsel at their own expense.

parameters.start_event: date registrar mails the agreement to arbitrate
parameters.effect_of_return: authorizes registrar to proceed with administrative arbitration

rules.applies_to: Owners/complainants and licensed contractors in voluntary CSLB arbitration (B&P 7085(a) cases)
rules.verbatim_quote: The registrar shall forward an “agreement to arbitrate” to the complainant and the licensee. This agreement shall be returned to the registrar within 30 calendar days of the date that the agreement is mailed by the registrar.
rules.notes: Voluntary track. For the mandatory track (7085(b)) see B&P 7085.4(b).

rules.title: Mandatory arbitration notice: 30 days; complainant non-return closes complaint
rules.plain_english: In mandatory arbitration cases, CSLB mails a notice to arbitrate to both parties, due back within 30 calendar days of mailing. If the owner/complainant does not return it, the complaint is closed. If the contractor does not return it, CSLB can still send the case to arbitration and enforce the award.

parameters.start_event: date registrar mails the notice to arbitrate
parameters.licensee_failure_to_return: does not stop referral to arbitration or enforcement of award under B&P 7085.6 (contested or noncontested hearing)

rules.applies_to: Owners/complainants and licensed contractors in mandatory CSLB arbitration (B&P 7085(b) cases)
rules.verbatim_quote: This notice shall be returned to the registrar within 30 calendar days of the date that the notice is mailed by the registrar. The complainant’s failure to return an executed copy of the notice shall result in the closure of the complaint.
rules.notes: Contractor non-response is not a defense; the hearing can proceed and the award is enforceable.

rules.title: Required contents of a CSLB agreement to arbitrate; board pays fee
rules.plain_english: Every CSLB agreement to arbitrate must list each party's name, address and phone number, the issue in dispute, and the dollar amount or other remedy sought. The arbitration fee is paid by CSLB from the Contractors License Fund, not by the parties.

required_fields: amount in dollars or other remedy sought

rules.applies_to: Parties to CSLB arbitration
rules.verbatim_quote: All “agreements to arbitrate” shall include the names, addresses, and telephone numbers of the parties to the dispute, the issue in dispute, and the amount in dollars or any other remedy sought. The appropriate fee shall be paid by the board from the Contractors License Fund.

rules.title: Strike and rank arbitrator list within 7 days
rules.plain_english: Each party gets the same list of possible arbitrators and has 7 days from the mailing date to cross off objectionable names, rank the rest, and return it. If you do not return it on time, every name on the list is treated as acceptable to you. One arbitrator hears the case unless CSLB or the association directs more.

parameters.start_event: mailing date of the arbitrator list
parameters.default_if_not_returned: all persons on list deemed acceptable
parameters.mandatory_cases: in B&P 7085(b) cases the board/association may appoint the arbitrator directly (7085.5(b)(2))

rules.applies_to: Parties to voluntary CSLB arbitration
rules.verbatim_quote: Each party to the dispute shall have seven days from the mailing date in which to cross off any names to which it objects, number the remaining names to indicate the order of preference, and return the list to the board or appointed arbitration association. If a party does not return the list within the time specified, all persons named in the list are acceptable.
rules.notes: Statute does not say calendar vs. working days for this 7-day period; treat as calendar days conservatively.

rules.title: Arbitrator must have no interest and must disclose bias
rules.plain_english: A person with a financial or personal interest in the outcome cannot be the arbitrator. Before accepting, the arbitrator must disclose anything that could delay the hearing or suggest bias; CSLB or the association then replaces the arbitrator or asks the parties for comment, and its disqualification decision is conclusive.

parameters.decision_on_disqualification: board or appointed arbitration association; conclusive

rules.applies_to: Parties to CSLB arbitration
rules.verbatim_quote: No person shall serve as an arbitrator in any arbitration in which that person has any financial or personal interest in the result of the arbitration. Prior to accepting an appointment, the prospective arbitrator shall disclose any circumstances likely to prevent a prompt hearing or to create a presumption of bias.

rules.title: Respond with convenient hearing dates within 7 calendar days
rules.plain_english: In voluntary arbitration, CSLB or the association sends a list of hearing times, dates and locations. Each party must tell the arbitrator which work for them within 7 calendar days of mailing, or the arbitrator sets the hearing. The arbitrator may inspect the jobsite and any party may attend the inspection.

parameters.start_event: mailing of the list of hearing times/dates/locations
parameters.default_if_no_response: arbitrator fixes time, place, and location
parameters.site_inspection: at arbitrator's sole discretion; parties notified; any party may be present
parameters.mandatory_cases: in B&P 7085(b) cases the board/association fixes the hearing time and place (7085.5(e)(2))

rules.applies_to: Parties to CSLB arbitration
rules.verbatim_quote: The parties shall notify the arbitrator, within seven calendar days of the mailing of the list, of the times and dates convenient to each party. If the parties fail to respond to the arbitrator within the seven-day period, the arbitrator shall fix the time, place, and location of the hearing.

rules.title: No transcript required; party may pay for its own record
rules.plain_english: CSLB arbitration hearings do not have to be recorded. A party who wants a record (court reporter, etc.) can arrange one at its own expense, and parties may take notes. Hearings are adjourned only for good cause, and people with a direct interest may attend.

parameters.attendance: any person with direct interest; arbitrator may exclude non-party witnesses during other testimony

rules.applies_to: Parties to CSLB arbitration
rules.verbatim_quote: A record is not required to be taken of the proceedings. However, any party to the proceeding may have a record made at its own expense. The parties may make appropriate notes of the proceedings.

rules.title: Arbitration hearing order: complainant first, then defense
rules.plain_english: The arbitrator sets the schedule for document exchange and witness lists. At the hearing the complaining party presents its claims, proof and witnesses first, then the defending party presents its defenses; witnesses can be questioned. The arbitrator decides what evidence is relevant and formal rules of evidence do not apply.
rules.applies_to: Parties to CSLB arbitration
rules.verbatim_quote: The complaining party shall present its claims, proofs, and witnesses, who shall submit to questions or other examination. The defending party shall then present its defenses, proofs, and witnesses, who shall submit to questions or other examination.
rules.notes: Arbitrator may vary the procedure but must give full and equal opportunity to present proofs.

rules.title: Arbitration can proceed if a party does not show up
rules.plain_english: If a party gets proper notice and does not appear, the arbitration can go forward without them. The attending party must still prove its case with evidence; an award cannot be based only on the other side's failure to appear.

parameters.condition: party fails to appear after due notice

rules.applies_to: Parties to CSLB arbitration
rules.verbatim_quote: The arbitration may proceed in the absence of any party who, after due notice, fails to be present. The arbitrator shall require the attending party to submit supporting evidence in order to make an award.

rules.title: Pre-hearing documents must be copied to all parties at the same time
rules.plain_english: You may submit documents to the arbitrator before the hearing, but you must send a copy at the same time to every other party and to CSLB or the arbitration association.
rules.applies_to: Parties to CSLB arbitration
rules.verbatim_quote: Documents to be considered by the arbitrator may be submitted prior to the hearing. However, a copy shall be simultaneously transmitted to all other parties and to the board or appointed arbitration association for transmittal to the arbitrator or board appointed arbitrator.

rules.title: When the arbitration hearing is deemed closed
rules.plain_english: The hearing closes when the parties say they have no more proof. If briefs are allowed, it closes on the brief due date; if documents are due later than briefs, it closes on the later date. The 30-day clock for the award starts at closing. The arbitrator can reopen the hearing on its own motion.

parameters.close_event_default: parties confirm no further proofs or witnesses
parameters.close_event_if_briefs: final date set for receipt of briefs
parameters.close_event_if_later_documents: later date set for receipt of documents
parameters.award_clock_starts: closing of the hearings (absent other agreement)

rules.applies_to: Parties to CSLB arbitration
rules.verbatim_quote: The time limit within which the arbitrator is required to make the award shall commence to run, in the absence of other agreements by the parties, upon the closing of the hearings.

rules.title: Object in writing within 10 calendar days of hearing close or waive
rules.plain_english: If you know a CSLB arbitration rule was not followed and you continue anyway, you must give the arbitrator a written objection within 10 calendar days after the hearing closes, or you lose the right to object.

parameters.start_event: close of hearing

rules.applies_to: Parties to CSLB arbitration
rules.verbatim_quote: Any party who proceeds with the arbitration after knowledge that any provision or requirement of these rules has not been complied with, and who fails to state their objections to the arbitrator in writing, within 10 calendar days of close of hearing, shall be deemed to have waived their right to object.

rules.title: How arbitration papers are served; certified mail to non-responding contractor
rules.plain_english: Arbitration papers (including for court actions and judgment entry) may be served by regular mail to the party or its attorney at the last known address, or by personal service. In mandatory cases where the contractor did not return the notice to arbitrate, papers including the hearing notice go by certified mail to the contractor's CSLB address of record, so keep that address current.

default_methods: regular mail to party or attorney at last known address
parameters.mandatory_case_nonresponsive_contractor: certified mail to contractor's address of record
parameters.award_service: certified mail to last known address/address of record, or personal service (7085.5(t))

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors and complainants in CSLB arbitration
rules.verbatim_quote: in all cases referred to arbitration pursuant to subdivision (b) of Section 7085 in which the contractor fails or refuses to return an executed copy of the notice to arbitrate within the time specified, any papers or process specified in paragraph (1) to be sent to the contractor, including the notice of hearing, shall be mailed by certified mail to the contractor’s address of record.
rules.notes: Practical check: a contractor's address of record with CSLB must be current, or the contractor may miss hearing notices that are still legally effective.

rules.title: Arbitrator must issue award within 30 calendar days of close
rules.plain_english: Unless the parties agree otherwise, the arbitrator must issue the award no later than 30 calendar days after the hearing (or reopened hearing) closes, or after final statements are sent if the oral hearing was waived. The arbitrator can extend other deadlines for good cause, but not the award deadline.

start_event_options: transmittal of final statements and proofs if oral hearing waived

rules.applies_to: CSLB arbitration (useful for parties tracking award timing)
rules.verbatim_quote: The award shall be made promptly by the arbitrator, and unless otherwise agreed by the parties, no later than 30 calendar days from the date of closing the hearing, closing a reopened hearing, or if oral hearing has been waived, from the date of transmitting the final statements and proofs to the arbitrator.

rules.title: Arbitrator may award any just remedy, costs, and repair costs
rules.plain_english: The CSLB arbitrator can order any remedy that is just and equitable within the scope of the referral, may award costs or expenses at its discretion, and may award the owner all direct costs and expenses to complete or repair the project.

parameters.remedy_scope: any remedy or relief just and equitable, within scope of board referral
parameters.complainant_recoverable: all direct costs and expenses for completion or repair of the project

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors and owners in CSLB arbitration
rules.verbatim_quote: The arbitrator may grant any remedy or relief that the arbitrator deems just and equitable and within the scope of the board’s referral and the requirements of the board. The arbitrator, in their sole discretion, may award costs or expenses.

rules.title: Arbitration award becomes final 30 calendar days after issuance
rules.plain_english: A CSLB arbitration award becomes final 30 calendar days after the date it is issued. The award must be in writing and signed by the arbitrator (or a majority).

parameters.start_event: date arbitration award is issued
parameters.form: in writing, signed by arbitrator or majority

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors and owners in CSLB arbitration
rules.verbatim_quote: The award shall become final 30 calendar days from the date the arbitration award is issued.
rules.notes: Calculation: final_date = issue_date + 30 calendar days; court appeal deadline = final_date + 30 calendar days (see arbitration-award-court-appeal-30-days).

rules.title: Ask to correct a clerical/math error in the award within 10 days
rules.plain_english: A party can ask the arbitrator to fix an obvious miscalculation, a wrong description of a person or property, or another clerical error by serving a written application on the arbitrator and all parties within 10 calendar days of service of the award. Others may object within 10 calendar days of service of the application. The arbitrator must deny or correct within 30 calendar days of service of the original award.

parameters.application_start_event: date of service of the award
parameters.objection_start_event: date of service of the application for correction
parameters.arbitrator_decision_start_event: date of service of the original award
allowed_grounds: evident mistake in description of person, thing, or property
other clerical error not affecting the merits

rules.applies_to: Parties to CSLB arbitration
rules.verbatim_quote: An application for correction of the award shall be made within 10 calendar days of the date of service of the award by serving a copy of the application on the arbitrator, and all other parties to the arbitration.
rules.notes: Correction is limited to clerical issues; merits disputes require a court appeal.

rules.title: Appeal an arbitration award to court within 30 days after it is final
rules.plain_english: To challenge a CSLB arbitration award (or a denial/correction), file in a court of competent jurisdiction and file a true copy with the arbitrator or arbitration association within 30 calendar days after the award becomes final. If no appeal is filed, the award becomes a final order of the Registrar.

parameters.start_event: date award becomes final (issue date + 30 calendar days)
file_with: true copy to arbitrator or appointed arbitration association
parameters.if_no_appeal: becomes final order of the registrar

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors and owners in CSLB arbitration
rules.verbatim_quote: Any appeal from the denial or correction shall be filed with a court of competent jurisdiction and a true copy thereof shall be filed with the arbitrator or appointed arbitration association within 30 calendar days after the award has become final.
rules.notes: effective_deadline_from_issue_date_days is derived (30 + 30), not stated in the text. Service of the award by certified mail is effective when mailed to the party's last known address or address of record (7085.5(t)). Literal text: "Any appeal from the denial or correction shall be filed with a court of competent jurisdiction ... within 30 calendar days after the award has become final"; the next sentence ("If no appeal is filed within the 30-calendar day period, it shall become a final order of the registrar") shows the same window governs a challenge to the award itself.

verification.correction: No error. 30 calendar days after the award becomes final, filing with court plus true copy to arbitrator/association, and final-order effect confirmed. Added a note quoting the exact appeal sentence, which names "the denial or correction".

rules.title: CSLB pays for one expert on unrepaired workmanship issues
rules.plain_english: If either party asks for an expert and the case involves workmanship problems itemized in the complaint that have not been repaired or replaced, CSLB pays for one board-appointed expert (site inspection, report, and hearing appearance). A party who brings its own additional expert pays for that expert.

covered_costs: fees for appearing or testifying at hearing
parameters.payment_request: registrar-approved form; board approves before payment

rules.applies_to: Owners and contractors in CSLB arbitration with workmanship disputes
rules.verbatim_quote: The board shall pay the expenses of one expert witness appointed by the board when the services of an expert witness are requested by either party involved in arbitration pursuant to this article and the case involves workmanship issues that are itemized in the complaint and have not been repaired or replaced.
rules.notes: A software tool advising an owner should note: itemize workmanship defects in the complaint and do not repair them before the expert inspects if the free expert is wanted.

rules.title: Parties consent to court judgment on the arbitration award
rules.plain_english: By participating in CSLB arbitration, the parties are deemed to consent that a judgment on the award may be entered in any federal or state court with jurisdiction. CSLB, the association and the arbitrator are not necessary parties to court proceedings and are not liable for their acts in the arbitration.

parameters.courts: any federal or state court having jurisdiction

rules.applies_to: Parties to CSLB arbitration
rules.verbatim_quote: Parties to these rules shall be deemed to have consented that judgment upon the arbitration award may be entered in any federal or state court having jurisdiction thereof.

rules.title: Not complying with an arbitration award: suspension in 30 days; appeal in 15
rules.plain_english: If a contractor does not comply with a CSLB arbitration award, the license is automatically suspended. CSLB sends a certified-mail notice and the suspension takes effect 30 calendar days from the notice date. The contractor may appeal the suspension in writing within 15 calendar days after service of the notice.

parameters.trigger: licensee fails to comply with arbitration award

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors subject to a CSLB arbitration award
rules.verbatim_quote: The registrar shall notify the licensee by certified mail of the failure to comply with the arbitrator’s award, and that the license shall be automatically suspended 30 calendar days from the date of that notice. (3) The licensee may appeal the suspension for noncompliance within 15 calendar days after service of the notice by written notice to the registrar.
rules.notes: Additional licenses held or qualified by the licensee may also be suspended without further notice (B&P 7097).

rules.title: Award still unpaid 90 days after suspension: all licenses revoked
rules.plain_english: A contractor suspended for not complying with an arbitration award can be reinstated at any time by complying. If not reinstated within 90 days of the suspension, that license and every other contractor license issued to the licensee are automatically revoked for a period set under B&P 7102. The Registrar may delay revocation for good cause up to 1 year if the licensee applies in writing before the revocation date.

parameters.reinstatement: any time by complying with award and registrar's final order
parameters.revocation_scope: the license and any other contractor's license issued to the licensee
parameters.delay_request: written application to registrar before revocation date, stating good cause

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors subject to a CSLB arbitration award
rules.verbatim_quote: If no reinstatement of the license is made within 90 days of the date of the automatic suspension, the license and any other contractor’s license issued to the licensee shall be automatically revoked by operation of law for a period to be determined by the registrar pursuant to Section 7102.
rules.notes: Registrar's power to grant a delay expires on the effective date of the revocation.

rules.title: Award non-complier barred from other licenses; replace qualifier in 90 days
rules.plain_english: A licensee suspended for not complying with an arbitration award is automatically barred from being an officer, director, partner, manager, associate or qualifier of another licensee. If that person was another company's qualifier, the other company must replace the qualifier within 90 days of disassociation or its license is suspended or the qualifier's classification removed.

parameters.employing_barred_person: grounds for discipline of the other licensee
parameters.start_event: date of disassociation
parameters.failure_consequence: other licensee's license automatically suspended or qualifier's classification removed

rules.applies_to: Contracting companies whose officers/qualifiers have unpaid CSLB arbitration awards
rules.verbatim_quote: A qualifier disassociated pursuant to this section shall be replaced within 90 days from the date of disassociation. Upon failure to replace the qualifier within 90 days of the disassociation, the license of the other licensee shall be automatically suspended or the qualifier’s classification removed at the end of the 90 days.

rules.title: Owner can enforce the arbitration award in court
rules.plain_english: The complainant (for example, the owner) may enforce a CSLB arbitrator's award in court using the Code of Civil Procedure arbitration-award procedures beginning at CCP 1285.

parameters.procedure: Code of Civil Procedure Part 3, Title 9, Chapter 2 (commencing with Section 1285)

rules.applies_to: Owners/complainants holding a CSLB arbitration award
rules.verbatim_quote: A complainant may enforce an arbitrator’s award in accordance with Chapter 2 (commencing with Section 1285) of Title 9 of Part 3 of the Code of Civil Procedure.
rules.notes: This is in addition to the licensing consequences of non-compliance under B&P 7085.6.

rules.title: Complaints sent to arbitration are not public unless award is ignored
rules.plain_english: A complaint referred to CSLB arbitration is not disclosed to the public unless and until CSLB opens an investigation into the contractor's failure to comply with the arbitration award.

parameters.disclosure_trigger: registrar initiates investigation into alleged violation of B&P 7085.6 (award noncompliance)

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors; owners checking a contractor's CSLB record
rules.verbatim_quote: Notwithstanding any other provision of law, a complaint referred to arbitration pursuant to Section 7085 is not subject to disclosure to the public until such time as an investigation into an alleged violation of Section 7085.6 has been initiated by the registrar.
rules.notes: A clean public CSLB record does not rule out a pending arbitration.

rules.title: Solar Energy System Restitution Program has been repealed
rules.plain_english: The CSLB Solar Energy System Restitution Program (B&P 7086-7086.11), which paid restitution to certain solar customers, was repealed on June 30, 2024. A tool should not direct current claimants to it.
rules.applies_to: Solar contractors and solar customers
rules.verbatim_quote: Added Stats 2021 ch 77 § 1 (AB 137), effective July 16, 2021, repealed June 30, 2024.
rules.notes: Only section titles and history are printed; program text is not reproduced in the 2026 book. 7086.10 also amended by Stats 2022 ch 11 (SB 1495).

rules.title: CSLB must investigate a verified written complaint
rules.plain_english: The Registrar may investigate on its own and must investigate when any person files a verified written complaint against an applicant, contractor or home improvement salesperson. Outcomes can include denial or non-renewal, citation, temporary suspension or permanent revocation.

parameters.trigger: verified complaint in writing by any person

rules.applies_to: Owners filing complaints; contractors and HIS registrants
rules.verbatim_quote: The registrar may upon his or her own motion and shall upon the verified complaint in writing of any person, investigate the actions of any applicant, contractor, or home improvement salesperson within the state
rules.notes: Complaint filing deadlines are in B&P 7091.

rules.title: Licensees can be disciplined for conduct on otherwise-exempt projects
rules.plain_english: A licensed contractor (or applicant) can be disciplined even if the misconduct happened on a project or in a role that would otherwise be exempt from licensing under B&P 7044, 7045, 7046 or 7048 (for example, owner-builder or minor-work exemptions).
rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors and applicants, including when working as owner-builders or on small jobs
rules.verbatim_quote: even though the grounds or cause for such disciplinary action arose upon projects or while the applicant, licensee, or registrant was acting in a capacity or under circumstances or facts which, under the provisions of Sections 7044, 7045, 7046, and 7048, would otherwise exempt the person or his or her operations from the provisions of this chapter.
rules.notes: The content of the 7044-7048 exemptions is on earlier pages of the Law Book (previous chunks).

rules.title: Willful building permit violations require discipline (under-$500 equipment repair excepted)
rules.plain_english: If CSLB finds a contractor willfully and deliberately violated a state or local building permit law, the Registrar must take disciplinary action. Exceptions: not pulling a permit for repair, maintenance or adjustment of equipment valued under $500 for labor or materials, or for replacing a mechanical equipment part with an identical part.

parameters.trigger: willful and deliberate violation of state or local law relating to issuance of building permits
parameters.exception_scope: repair, maintenance, and adjustment of equipment
parameters.exception_identical_part: replacing a part/component part of mechanical equipment with the identical part

rules.applies_to: All licensed contractors doing permit-required work
rules.verbatim_quote: has willfully and deliberately violated any state or local law relating to the issuance of building permits, other than failure to obtain a county or city permit for repair, maintenance, and adjustment of equipment where such repair, maintenance, or adjustment is valued at less than five hundred dollars ($500) for labor or materials
rules.notes: Permit-law violations are also listed in B&P 7110(h), which carries the higher civil penalty range (up to $30,000) under B&P 7099.2. The $500 exception is only a CSLB-discipline exception; the local permit requirement may still apply.

rules.title: Work without a permit is presumed willful
rules.plain_english: For CSLB discipline, construction done without a required permit is presumed to be a willful and deliberate violation; the contractor must rebut it. In suspension/revocation proceedings, CSLB carries the burden of proof by clear and convincing evidence.

parameters.presumption: construction performed without a permit = willful and deliberate violation

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors
rules.verbatim_quote: For the purpose of this section, there shall be a rebuttable presumption affecting the burden of proof that construction performed without a permit is a willful and deliberate violation.
rules.notes: A permit tracker should flag every permit-required scope before work starts.

rules.title: Unpaid citation penalty or ignored correction order: auto suspension
rules.plain_english: Once a citation is final, failing to pay the civil penalty, to make the ordered correction, or to pay the ordered sum to the injured party automatically suspends the license 30 days after noncompliance. CSLB sends written notice that the license will be suspended 30 days from the notice date; the licensee may contest in writing within 15 days after service.

triggers: failure to comply with order of correction
failure to pay specified sum to injured party in lieu of correction

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors with a final citation
rules.verbatim_quote: the failure to pay a civil penalty, or to comply with an order of correction or an order to pay a specified sum to an injured party in lieu of correction once the order has become final, shall result in the automatic suspension of a license by operation of law 30 days after noncompliance with the terms of the order.
rules.notes: Additional licenses of the licensee may be suspended without further notice (B&P 7097).

rules.title: Citation still unmet 90 days after suspension: all licenses revoked
rules.plain_english: A license suspended for not complying with a final citation can be reinstated any time by complying. If not reinstated within 90 days of suspension, the cited license and all other contractor licenses issued to the licensee are automatically revoked for a period set under B&P 7102. Revocation can be delayed for good cause up to 1 year on a written request filed before the revocation date.

parameters.revocation_scope: cited license and any other contractors' license issued to the licensee
parameters.delay_request: written application before revocation date stating good cause

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors with a final citation
rules.verbatim_quote: If no reinstatement of the license is made within 90 days of the date of the automatic suspension, the cited license and any other contractors’ license issued to the licensee shall be automatically revoked by operation of law for a period to be determined by the registrar pursuant to Section 7102.

rules.title: Citation non-complier barred from other licenses; replace qualifier in 90 days
rules.plain_english: A cited licensee who does not comply is automatically barred from serving as officer, director, associate, partner, manager or qualifier of another licensee. If they qualified another license, that licensee must replace the qualifier within 90 days or face automatic suspension or loss of the qualifier's classification.

parameters.start_event: date of disassociation
parameters.failure_consequence: other licensee's license automatically suspended or qualifier's classification removed

rules.applies_to: Contracting companies whose officers/qualifiers have uncomplied citations
rules.verbatim_quote: A qualifier disassociated pursuant to this section shall be replaced within 90 days of the date of disassociation. Upon failure to replace the qualifier within 90 days of the prohibition, the license of the other licensee shall be automatically suspended or the qualifier’s classification removed at the end of the 90 days.

rules.title: Fixing the problem does not excuse fraud or repeated violations
rules.plain_english: If a contractor commits a fraudulent act (B&P 7116), correcting the resulting condition does not by itself stop CSLB discipline. Likewise, a contractor who repeatedly avoids discipline by fixing each problem can still be disciplined for the pattern.
rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors
rules.verbatim_quote: In the event a licensee commits a fraudulent act which is a ground for disciplinary action under Section 7116 of this article, the correction of any condition resulting from such act shall not in and of itself preclude the registrar from taking disciplinary action under this article.

rules.title: CSLB complaint for visible (patent) problems: 4 years
rules.plain_english: A complaint to CSLB about patent (obvious) acts or omissions must be filed in writing within 4 years after the act or omission. CSLB must then file the disciplinary action or refer to arbitration within 4 years after the act or within 18 months after the complaint was filed, whichever is later.

parameters.action_deadline_rule: later of (act + 4 years) or (complaint filing date + 18 months)

rules.applies_to: Owners/complainants and licensed contractors
rules.verbatim_quote: A complaint against a licensee alleging commission of any patent acts or omissions that may be grounds for legal action shall be filed in writing with the registrar within four years after the act or omission alleged as the ground for the disciplinary action.
rules.notes: These are CSLB administrative deadlines, not civil statutes of limitation. Surety-bond limitation periods are not affected (7091(g)).

rules.title: CSLB complaint for hidden (latent) structural defects: 10 years
rules.plain_english: A complaint about latent structural defects (willful departure from trade standards under B&P 7109(a)) must be filed in writing within 10 years after the act or omission. CSLB must file its action within 10 years after the act or within 18 months after the complaint, whichever is later. Latent means not apparent by reasonable inspection.

parameters.action_deadline_rule: later of (act + 10 years) or (complaint filing date + 18 months)
parameters.defect_type: latent structural defect, as defined by regulation
parameters.latent_definition: act or omission not apparent by reasonable inspection

rules.applies_to: Owners/complainants and licensed contractors
rules.verbatim_quote: A complaint against a licensee alleging commission of any latent acts or omissions that may be grounds for legal action pursuant to subdivision (a) of Section 7109 regarding structural defects, as defined by regulation, shall be filed in writing with the registrar within 10 years after the act or omission alleged as the ground for the disciplinary action.
rules.notes: Structural defect definition is in CSLB regulations (not on these pages).

rules.title: License fraud and criminal conviction actions: 2 years from discovery
rules.plain_english: CSLB must file discipline for application misrepresentation (B&P 7112) within 2 years after CSLB discovers the facts, and for a criminal conviction (B&P 7123) within 2 years after CSLB discovers the conviction.

parameters.start_event: discovery by the registrar or board

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors
rules.verbatim_quote: A disciplinary action alleging a violation of Section 7112 shall be filed within two years after the discovery by the registrar or by the board of the alleged facts constituting the fraud or misrepresentation prohibited by the section.

rules.title: Breach of written warranty: CSLB action up to 18 months after warranty expires
rules.plain_english: CSLB can discipline a contractor for breaching an express written warranty the contractor issued, as long as the action is filed no later than 18 months after the warranty expires.

parameters.start_event: expiration of the express written warranty
parameters.warranty_type: express, written, issued by the contractor

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors who issue written warranties; owners holding them
rules.verbatim_quote: A disciplinary action regarding an alleged breach of an express, written warranty issued by the contractor shall be filed not later than 18 months from the expiration of the warranty.
rules.notes: A warranty tracker can compute CSLB exposure end date = warranty expiration + 18 months.

rules.title: What a CSLB disciplinary decision can order
rules.plain_english: A CSLB decision can immediately suspend all contracting operations for a set period, allow the contractor to finish specific uncompleted contracts, impose specific conditions (and refuse license restoration until met), or stay the decision during probation.

options: immediate complete suspension of all operations for fixed period
permit completion of uncompleted contracts shown at hearing
specific terms and conditions; no restoration application accepted until met
stay of execution pending probation terms

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors subject to accusation/discipline
rules.verbatim_quote: Provide for the immediate complete suspension by the licensee of all operations as a contractor during the period fixed by the decision. (2) Permit the licensee to complete any or all contracts shown by competent evidence taken at the hearing to be then uncompleted.
rules.notes: Owners with active projects should verify whether a suspended contractor was permitted to complete their contract.

rules.title: Probation violation can end a stayed suspension/revocation without notice
rules.plain_english: If a disciplinary decision is stayed on probation, failing to fully meet the probation terms may automatically terminate the stay without further notice, and the decision then counts as a disciplinary action.

parameters.trigger: failure to fully comply with probation terms
parameters.result: automatic termination of stay of execution

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors on CSLB probation
rules.verbatim_quote: Failure to fully comply with the terms and conditions of probation set pursuant to subparagraph (A) may result in automatic termination of the stay of execution without further notice.

rules.title: Discipline conditions: restitution, enforcement costs, coursework, exams
rules.plain_english: Conditions in a CSLB disciplinary decision or probation can include paying restitution to injured people, paying CSLB's investigation and enforcement costs (B&P 125.3), completing administrative or trade coursework, passing the law and business or trade exam, and other terms in CSLB disciplinary guidelines (16 CCR 871).

possible_conditions: law and business examination or trade examination

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors subject to discipline/probation
rules.verbatim_quote: Payment of restitution to persons injured as a result of the violation. (2) Payment of the costs of investigation and enforcement pursuant to Section 125.3. (3) Enrollment in, and completion of, specified administrative or trade-specific coursework.
rules.notes: Amended by SB 630 (Stats 2023 ch 153).

rules.title: Licensee includes the entity and its qualifying individuals
rules.plain_english: For CSLB discipline, a licensee is not just the business (individual, partnership, corporation, LLC, joint venture) but also its named RMO, RMM, responsible managing member, or other personnel whose qualifications got the license issued.
rules.applies_to: All licensed contracting businesses and their qualifiers
rules.verbatim_quote: shall also include any named responsible managing officer, responsible managing manager, responsible managing member, or personnel of that licentiate whose appearance has qualified the licentiate under the provisions of Section 7068.

rules.title: One license suspended: other licenses can be suspended without notice
rules.plain_english: When a license is suspended by CSLB decision, for a judgment/bond issue under B&P 7071.17(b), for ignoring an arbitration award (7085.6), or for ignoring a citation (7090.1), any other license in the licensee's name or that the person qualified can be suspended without further notice.

affected_licenses: licenses for which licensee furnished qualifying experience/appearance under B&P 7068

rules.applies_to: Licensees and qualifiers holding or qualifying multiple licenses
rules.verbatim_quote: any additional license issued under this chapter in the name of the licensee or for which the licensee furnished qualifying experience and appearance under the provisions of Section 7068, may be suspended by the registrar without further notice.
rules.notes: A subcontractor-vetting tool should check related licenses that share a qualifier.

rules.title: One license revoked: other licenses can be revoked without notice
rules.plain_english: When any license is revoked, any other license in the licensee's name or that the licensee qualified can be revoked without further notice.

affected_licenses: licenses qualified by licensee under B&P 7068

rules.applies_to: Licensees and qualifiers holding or qualifying multiple licenses
rules.verbatim_quote: when any license has been revoked under the provisions of this chapter, any additional license issued under this chapter in the name of the licensee or for which the licensee furnished qualifying experience and appearance under the provisions of Section 7068, may be revoked by the registrar without further notice.

rules.title: What a CSLB citation contains
rules.plain_english: Instead of formal discipline, CSLB can issue a written citation that describes the violation and the law violated. It may include an order to correct within a reasonable time, an order (licensees only) to pay a specified sum to the injured party instead of correcting, and a civil penalty.

parameters.form: in writing, describing violation with particularity and citing provisions violated
possible_orders: order of correction with reasonable time to correct
order to pay specified sum to injured party in lieu of correction (licensee only)

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors and license applicants
rules.verbatim_quote: In addition, each citation may contain an order of correction fixing a reasonable time for correction of the violation or an order, against the licensee only, for payment of a specified sum to an injured party in lieu of correction, and may contain an assessment of a civil penalty.

verification.checked_against: 2026 CSLB Law Book (sources/lawbook.txt), PDF page 339 (B&P 7099; B&P 7099.1)

rules.title: Citation civil penalty caps before July 1, 2026
rules.plain_english: For citations under the version in effect until July 1, 2026, the civil penalty could not exceed $8,000, except up to $30,000 for violating B&P 7110 (willful violation of building/labor/safety laws), 7114 (aiding unlicensed persons) or 7118 (contracting with an unlicensed contractor). No minimum was set.
rules.applies_to: Licensees/applicants cited for violations under the pre-July 2026 version
rules.verbatim_quote: a civil penalty shall not be assessed in an amount greater than eight thousand dollars ($8,000). Notwithstanding Section 125.9, a civil penalty not to exceed thirty thousand dollars ($30,000) may be assessed for a violation of Section 7110, 7114, or 7118.
rules.notes: Superseded by the July 1, 2026 version with minimums. Stats 2025 ch 455 (SB 291) prevails over ch 233.

verification.checked_against: 2026 CSLB Law Book (sources/lawbook.txt), PDF page 340 (B&P 7099.2 [Repealed effective July 1, 2026])

rules.title: Citation civil penalty ranges from July 1, 2026: $500-$8,000; $1,500-$30,000
rules.plain_english: Starting July 1, 2026, a CSLB citation civil penalty must be at least $500 and no more than $8,000. For violations of B&P 7110, 7114 or 7118 (willful violation of building/labor/safety laws, aiding unlicensed persons, contracting with unlicensed contractors), it must be at least $1,500 and no more than $30,000.
rules.applies_to: Licensees and applicants cited by CSLB
rules.verbatim_quote: a civil penalty shall be assessed in an amount not less than five hundred dollars ($500) nor greater than eight thousand dollars ($8,000). Notwithstanding Section 125.9, a civil penalty shall be assessed in an amount not less than one thousand five hundred dollars ($1,500) nor greater than thirty thousand dollars ($30,000) for a violation of Section 7110, 7114, or 7118.
rules.effective: Effective January 1, 2026; operative July 1, 2026 (Stats 2025 ch 455 § 2.2, SB 291, which prevails over Stats 2025 ch 233 § 4, SB 779)
rules.notes: Unlicensed-contractor citations are governed separately (B&P 7028.7 et seq., earlier pages). Some sections (e.g., 7125.4 workers' comp) set their own minimums. Penalties cannot be paid from the contractor's license bond (7099.7).

verification.checked_against: 2026 CSLB Law Book (sources/lawbook.txt), PDF page 340 (B&P 7099.2(b)(1) [Operative July 1, 2026])

rules.title: Minimum civil penalties may be CPI-adjusted every 5 years
rules.plain_english: CSLB may raise the minimum citation penalties for inflation every 5 years based on the California CPI increase since the subdivision took effect. Increases are rounded to multiples of $100 for penalties over $100 up to $1,000, and to multiples of $1,000 for penalties over $1,000.

parameters.index: Consumer Price Index per Revenue and Taxation Code 2212
parameters.base_period: CPI "at the time this subdivision goes into effect" (statutory wording). The section is effective January 1, 2026 but operative July 1, 2026; the statute does not say which date is the base. July 1, 2026 is an interpretation.

rules.applies_to: Licensees and applicants cited by CSLB
rules.verbatim_quote: The board may adjust all minimum civil penalties imposed by this section for inflation every five years. The adjustment shall be equivalent to the percentage, if any, that the Consumer Price Index, as determined pursuant to Section 2212 of the Revenue and Taxation Code, exceeds the Consumer Price Index at the time this subdivision goes into effect.
rules.effective: Effective January 1, 2026; operative July 1, 2026 (Stats 2025 ch 455 § 2.2, SB 291, which prevails)
rules.notes: Earliest possible adjustment would be about 2031; check CSLB for current minimums before calculating. Base date for the CPI comparison is ambiguous (effective Jan 1, 2026 vs operative July 1, 2026); confirm with CSLB before computing adjusted minimums.

"effective" said "July 1, 2026"; the book says effective January 1, 2026, operative July 1, 2026. base_period stated July 1, 2026 as fact; the text only says "at the time this subdivision goes into effect", which is ambiguous here. Flagged as an interpretation.

rules.title: Contest a CSLB citation within 15 days of service (B&P 7099.8(a); 7099.3 says 15 working days)
rules.plain_english: B&P 7099.3 lets a cited licensee or applicant appeal to the Registrar within 15 working days from service of the citation, challenging the alleged violations, correction periods, penalty amounts, or reasonableness of the required correction, and 7099.5 requires an APA hearing if the citation is contested. But B&P 7099.8(a), which applies "notwithstanding any other law" to citations under 7099, requires a written request for an administrative hearing within 15 days after service, and it does not say working days. Treat 15 calendar days from service as the deadline.

parameters.day_type: calendar days (safe reading; B&P 7099.8(a) says "within 15 days" and applies "notwithstanding any other law")
parameters.start_event: service of the citation
appealable_items: reasonableness of change required to correct
parameters.hearing: APA hearing (Gov Code 11500 et seq.) under B&P 7099.5; decision affirms, modifies, or vacates

overriding_rule_b_p_7099_8.text_controls: B&P 7099.8(a) applies "notwithstanding any other law" to citations under 7099
overriding_rule_b_p_7099_8.informal_conference_alternative: written request to chief of enforcement division within 15 days after service (7099.8(b))

parameters.safe_deadline: 15 calendar days after service of the citation

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors and applicants served with a citation
rules.verbatim_quote: Any licensee or applicant for licensure served with a citation pursuant to Section 7099, may appeal to the registrar within 15 working days from service of the citation with respect to violations alleged by the registrar, correction periods, amount of penalties, and the reasonableness of the change required by the registrar to correct the condition.
rules.notes: Do not compute this deadline in working days. 7099.8 (added 2019, amended 2020) is later and says "notwithstanding any other law"; 15 calendar days after service is the safe date.

verification.checked_against: 2026 CSLB Law Book (sources/lawbook.txt), PDF pages 341-342 (B&P 7099.3, 7099.5) and PDF pages 342-343 (B&P 7099.8)
verification.correction: The 7099.3 quote ("15 working days") is accurate, but the title and parameters treated 15 working days as the deadline. B&P 7099.8(a) (PDF page 342): "Notwithstanding any other law, if a person cited pursuant to Section 7028.7 or 7099 wishes to contest the citation, that person shall, within 15 days after service of the citation, file in writing a request for an administrative hearing". It does not say working days. Set day_type to calendar (safe reading), kept the 7099.3 working-day figure as b_p_7099_3_text_working_days, added the 7099.8 override, retitled the rule and rewrote the plain_english and notes. Same correction as the prior verified chunk made for 7028.10.

rules.title: Uncontested citation becomes final and unreviewable
rules.plain_english: Under B&P 7099.4, if the cited person does not notify CSLB within 15 working days of service that they intend to contest, the citation becomes a final order of the Registrar and cannot be reviewed by any court or agency; the Registrar may extend the 15-day period for cause. But B&P 7099.8(a) ("notwithstanding any other law") requires the written hearing request within 15 days after service, so do not rely on the working-day count: file within 15 calendar days.

parameters.start_event: service of the citation
parameters.result_if_missed: final order of registrar; not subject to review by any court or agency
parameters.safe_deadline: 15 calendar days after service of the citation (B&P 7099.8(a))

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors and applicants served with a citation
rules.verbatim_quote: If within 15 working days from service of the citation issued by the registrar, the licensee or applicant for licensure fails to notify the registrar that he or she intends to contest the citation, the citation shall be deemed a final order of the registrar and not be subject to review by any court or agency.
rules.notes: Once final, non-compliance triggers automatic suspension (7090.1) and is grounds for suspension/revocation (7099.6). B&P 7099.8(a) (PDF page 342) sets a 15-day (not working-day) deadline for a written hearing request "notwithstanding any other law"; the safe contest date is 15 calendar days after service.

verification.checked_against: 2026 CSLB Law Book (sources/lawbook.txt), PDF page 341 (B&P 7099.4) and PDF page 342 (B&P 7099.8(a))
verification.correction: 7099.4 quote, 15 working days, extension for cause and finality effect confirmed. The rule omitted B&P 7099.8(a), which applies "notwithstanding any other law" and requires a written hearing request within 15 days (not working days) after service. Relying on 15 working days could miss that deadline. Added the 7099.8(a) safe deadline to parameters, plain_english and notes.

rules.title: Ignoring a final citation: grounds for suspension, revocation, or denial
rules.plain_english: A licensee who fails to comply with a final citation can have the license suspended or revoked; an applicant who fails to comply can be denied a license.
rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors and applicants
rules.verbatim_quote: The failure of a licensee to comply with a citation after it is final is a ground for suspension or revocation of license.

rules.title: Civil penalties cannot be charged against the contractor's bond
rules.plain_english: CSLB cannot order a civil penalty to be paid from the contractor's license bond (B&P 7071.5-7071.8); the contractor pays it directly.
rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors and their sureties
rules.verbatim_quote: No order for payment of a civil penalty shall be made against any bond required pursuant to Sections 7071.5 to 7071.8.

rules.title: File written request for administrative hearing within 15 days of citation
rules.plain_english: Anyone cited by CSLB, licensed (B&P 7099) or unlicensed (B&P 7028.7), who wants to contest must file a written request for an administrative hearing within 15 days after service of the citation.

parameters.start_event: service of the citation

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors, applicants and unlicensed persons cited by CSLB
rules.verbatim_quote: if a person cited pursuant to Section 7028.7 or 7099 wishes to contest the citation, that person shall, within 15 days after service of the citation, file in writing a request for an administrative hearing as provided pursuant to Section 7028.12 or 7099.5.
rules.notes: Overlaps the 15 working-day periods in 7099.3/7099.4; calendar the shorter (15 calendar days) to be safe.

rules.title: Informal citation conference: request within 15 days; held within 60
rules.plain_english: Instead of or in addition to a hearing request, a cited person may ask in writing for an informal citation conference with the CSLB enforcement chief within 15 days after service. CSLB must hold it within 60 days of the request; the person may bring an attorney or representative. If held, the hearing request is deemed withdrawn, and any affirmed or modified citation (with reasons) is mailed within 10 days after the conference.

parameters.request_to: chief of the enforcement division or designee
parameters.representation: attorney or other authorized representative allowed

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors, applicants and unlicensed persons cited by CSLB
rules.verbatim_quote: Upon receipt of a written request for an informal citation conference, the chief of the enforcement division or a designee shall, within 60 days of the request, hold an informal citation conference with the person requesting the conference. The cited person may be accompanied and represented by an attorney or other authorized representative.

rules.title: Contest an affirmed/modified citation within 30 days
rules.plain_english: After an informal conference, if you still want to contest the affirmed or modified citation, you must submit a written request for an administrative hearing to the enforcement chief within 30 days after service of that citation. No second informal conference is allowed.

parameters.start_event: service of the modified or affirmed citation

rules.applies_to: Persons whose citation was affirmed or modified after an informal conference
rules.verbatim_quote: If a cited person wishes to contest a citation affirmed or modified pursuant to paragraph (3), the person shall, within 30 days after service of the modified or affirmed citation, contest the affirmed or modified citation by submitting a written request for an administrative hearing to the chief of the enforcement division or a designee.

rules.title: Letter of admonishment: respond within 30 days
rules.plain_english: CSLB may issue a letter of admonishment instead of a citation. Within 30 days of service you may either request an office conference in writing to contest it, or comply (and submit a written corrective action plan if required). Complying without requesting a conference is not an admission of the violation.

parameters.start_event: service of the letter of admonishment
options: written request for office conference to contest
comply and, if required, submit written corrective action plan

rules.applies_to: Licensees, HIS registrants and applicants receiving a letter of admonishment
rules.verbatim_quote: The letter of admonishment shall inform the licensee, registrant, or applicant that within 30 days of service of the letter of admonishment the licensee, registrant, or applicant may do either of the following:
rules.notes: Service by certified mail is effective on deposit in the mail (7099.9(c)), so the 30 days run from mailing.

rules.title: LOA office conference: decision in 14 days; writ within 30 days
rules.plain_english: At the office conference only your attorney or authorized representative may accompany you, and you may submit declarations and documents. CSLB may affirm, modify or withdraw the letter and must serve its written decision within 14 calendar days; that is the final administrative decision. Court review is by writ of mandate (CCP 1094.5) filed within 30 days after the decision is served or mailed.

parameters.who_may_accompany: legal counsel or authorized representative only
parameters.documents: declarations and documents may be submitted prior to or at conference
parameters.decision_service: personal service or certified mail to address of record
parameters.writ_start_event: date decision personally served or sent by certified mail
parameters.writ_procedure: petition for writ of mandate, CCP 1094.5

rules.applies_to: Licensees, HIS registrants and applicants contesting a letter of admonishment
rules.verbatim_quote: Within 14 calendar days from the date of the office conference, the registrar, or their designee, shall personally serve or send the written decision by certified mail to the licensee’s, registrant’s, or applicant’s address of record. This decision shall be deemed the final administrative decision concerning the letter of admonishment.

rules.title: LOA served by certified mail is effective when mailed
rules.plain_english: A letter of admonishment is served personally or by certified mail to your CSLB address of record, and certified-mail service is effective the day it is deposited in the U.S. mail, not when you receive it.

service_methods: certified mail to address of record
parameters.certified_mail_effective: upon deposit in United States mail

rules.applies_to: Licensees, HIS registrants and applicants
rules.verbatim_quote: The letter of admonishment shall be served upon the licensee, registrant, or applicant personally or by certified mail at their address of record with the board. If the licensee, registrant, or applicant is served by certified mail, service shall be effective upon deposit in the United States mail.
rules.notes: Keep the CSLB address of record current; deadlines run from mailing.

rules.title: Keep the letter of admonishment and corrective plan for 1 year
rules.plain_english: You must keep a copy of the letter of admonishment and any corrective action plan readily available for at least 1 year from the date the letter was issued.

parameters.start_event: date of issuance of the letter

rules.applies_to: Licensees, HIS registrants and applicants issued a letter of admonishment
rules.verbatim_quote: The licensee, registrant, or applicant shall maintain and have readily available a copy of the letter of admonishment and corrective action plan, if any, for at least one year from the date of issuance of the letter of admonishment.

rules.title: A letter of admonishment is not discipline
rules.plain_english: A letter of admonishment is not treated as a disciplinary action for licensing or discipline-reporting purposes, though it is publicly disclosed for 1 or 2 years (B&P 7124.6). CSLB keeps the power to cite or discipline instead.
rules.applies_to: Licensees, HIS registrants and applicants
rules.verbatim_quote: The issuance of a letter of admonishment shall not be construed as a disciplinary action or discipline for purposes of licensure or the reporting of discipline for licensure.

rules.title: When CSLB cannot use a letter of admonishment
rules.plain_english: CSLB may not resolve a case with a letter of admonishment if the person was unlicensed at the time, has a history of the same or similar violations, caused financial harm to someone, harmed an elder or dependent adult, or the violation involved repairing natural-disaster damage.

disqualifying_factors: history of same or similar violations
violation resulted in financial harm to another
victim is elder or dependent adult (Penal Code 368)
violation related to repair of natural disaster damage

rules.applies_to: Licensees, HIS registrants and applicants
rules.verbatim_quote: The board shall not issue a letter of admonishment when any one of the following factors is present: (1) The licensee, registrant, or applicant was unlicensed at the time of the violation. (2) The licensee, registrant, or applicant has a history of the same or similar violations. (3) The violation resulted in financial harm to another.
rules.notes: Disaster-repair and elder/dependent-adult jobs therefore carry at least citation-level exposure.

rules.title: Unlicensed directory ads: order to stop and disconnect phone numbers
rules.plain_english: If someone advertises construction work in an alphabetical or classified directory without being properly licensed (B&P 7027.1), CSLB can issue a citation ordering them to stop and to have the phone company disconnect every number in the ad, with no referral to a new number. A contested citation gets a hearing within 90 days; if the order is ignored after it is final, the PUC orders the phone service cut off.

parameters.trigger: advertising in alphabetical or classified directory without proper license (B&P 7027.1)
order_of_correction: notify telephone company to disconnect numbers in ad
no referral of calls to new number
parameters.noncompliance_after_final: registrar informs Public Utilities Commission, which requires disconnection

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors advertising outside their classification and unlicensed persons
rules.verbatim_quote: the registrar may issue a citation under Section 7099 containing an order of correction which requires the violator to cease the unlawful advertising and to notify the telephone company furnishing services to the violator to disconnect the telephone service furnished to any telephone number contained in the unlawful advertising
rules.notes: Advertising rules themselves (B&P 7027.1, 7030.5 license number in ads) are on earlier pages.

rules.title: Asbestos removal ads must show certification and registration numbers
rules.plain_english: You may not advertise asbestos removal unless you hold CSLB asbestos certification (B&P 7058.5) and Cal/OSHA registration (Labor Code 6501.5). Every ad must show both numbers and use the same name under which you are certified and registered. Missing numbers get a notice to comply; ignoring it, or advertising without valid certification/registration, gets a citation.

parameters.name_requirement: same name under which certified and registered
citation_triggers: advertising without valid certification and registration

rules.applies_to: Contractors advertising asbestos removal
rules.verbatim_quote: No person shall advertise, as that term is defined in Section 7027.1, to promote his or her services for the removal of asbestos unless he or she is certified to engage in asbestos-related work pursuant to Section 7058.5, and registered for that purpose pursuant to Section 6501.5 of the Labor Code. Each advertisement shall include that person’s certification and registration numbers
rules.notes: Category chosen because this dictates required advertisement text (not a contract).

rules.title: Bond of at least $1,000 to keep operating during court review
rules.plain_english: While a court reviews a CSLB decision, the court may let the contractor keep doing business only if the contractor posts a bond in an amount the court sets, at least the greater of $1,000 or what the court finds sufficient to protect the public. Without such a bond, there is no stay of CSLB's decision pending appeal.

parameters.bond_rule: greater of $1,000 or amount court finds sufficient to protect the public

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors seeking court review of CSLB discipline
rules.verbatim_quote: upon the filing of a proper bond by the licensee in an amount to be fixed by the court, but not less than one thousand dollars ($1,000) or an amount the court finds is sufficient to protect the public, whichever is greater

rules.title: Reinstatement after suspension requires proof of compliance
rules.plain_english: After a suspension, CSLB may reinstate the license once the contractor proves compliance with the decision's reinstatement terms; if the decision has none, reinstatement is at the Registrar's discretion.

parameters.requirement: proof of compliance with all reinstatement provisions of the decision

rules.applies_to: Suspended licensees
rules.verbatim_quote: After suspension of a license upon any of the grounds set forth in this chapter, the registrar may reinstate the license upon proof of compliance by the contractor with all provisions of the decision as to reinstatement

rules.title: After revocation: 1-5 year wait and all losses paid
rules.plain_english: A revoked license cannot be reinstated or reissued, and no license can go to personnel of the revoked licensee who knew of or took part in the violations, for at least 1 and up to 5 years after the final revocation decision. Even then, all losses caused must be fully satisfied and all conditions met. The wait can be extended based on gravity, prior violations and criminal convictions.

parameters.start_event: final decision of revocation
parameters.applies_to_personnel: members of personnel who had knowledge of or participated in the acts
preconditions: all loss caused by the act/omission fully satisfied
all conditions of revocation decision complied with

rules.applies_to: Revoked licensees and their officers/personnel; companies considering hiring them as qualifiers
rules.verbatim_quote: the license shall not be reinstated or reissued and a license shall not be issued to any member of the personnel of the revoked licensee found to have had knowledge of or participated in the acts or omissions constituting grounds for revocation, within a minimum period of one year and a maximum period of five years after the final decision of revocation

rules.title: Debts discharged in bankruptcy need not be paid to relicense
rules.plain_english: To be relicensed after revocation, a monetary debt from the violation does not have to be paid to the extent it was discharged in bankruptcy. Non-monetary conditions not discharged in bankruptcy must still be met first.
rules.applies_to: Revoked licensees seeking reissuance
rules.verbatim_quote: the satisfaction of the monetary obligation or debt as a prerequisite for the issuance, reissuance, or reinstatement of a license shall not be required to the extent the monetary obligation or debt was discharged in a bankruptcy proceeding.

rules.title: Discipline in another state is grounds for California discipline
rules.plain_english: If another state revokes, suspends or otherwise disciplines a person's contractor license, that is grounds for discipline of a California licensee or applicant; a certified copy of the other state's action is conclusive evidence.

parameters.trigger: revocation, suspension, or other disciplinary action by another state

rules.applies_to: California licensees and applicants licensed in other states
rules.verbatim_quote: The revocation, suspension, or other disciplinary action of a license to act as a contractor by another state shall constitute grounds for disciplinary action in this state if the individual is a licensee, or applies for a license, in this state.

rules.title: CSLB must tell the complainant (and contractor) how a complaint was resolved
rules.plain_english: When CSLB resolves a complaint it must notify the complainant in writing of its action and reasons, and send the same notice to the licensed contractor unless it would jeopardize an action or investigation.

notice_to: licensed contractor (unless it would jeopardize an action/investigation)

rules.applies_to: Owners/complainants and licensed contractors
rules.verbatim_quote: When the board resolves a complaint, the board shall notify the complainant in writing of its action and the reasons for taking that action. The board shall provide the same notice in writing to the contractor provided that the contractor is licensed and the notification would not jeopardize an action or investigation that involves the contractor.

rules.title: Letting a license lapse or surrendering it does not stop discipline
rules.plain_english: Expiration, cancellation, forfeiture, suspension, revocation or voluntary surrender of a license does not stop CSLB from investigating, prosecuting, or issuing a suspension or revocation decision. A court case about the contractor's performance can also include license suspension or revocation (B&P 7106).
rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors
rules.verbatim_quote: The expiration, cancellation, forfeiture, revocation, or suspension of a license by operation of law or by order or decision of the registrar or a court of law, or the voluntary surrender of a license by a licensee, shall not deprive the registrar of jurisdiction to proceed with any investigation of or action or disciplinary proceeding against the license

rules.title: Abandoning a project without legal excuse
rules.plain_english: Walking off a construction project without a legal excuse is grounds for CSLB discipline.

parameters.prohibited_act: abandonment of construction project or operation

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors
rules.verbatim_quote: Abandonment without legal excuse of any construction project or operation engaged in or undertaken by the licensee as a contractor constitutes a cause for disciplinary action.
rules.notes: Document any legal excuse (e.g., owner non-payment, stop-work notice) in writing before leaving a job.

rules.title: Diverting project funds or failing to account for them
rules.plain_english: Using money or property received for a specific project (or for a specific purpose on a project) for something else, or failing to substantially account for how those funds were used on that project, is grounds for discipline.

prohibited_acts: diversion of funds/property received for a specific project
diversion of funds received for a specified purpose on a project
failure to substantially account for application of such funds

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors receiving owner deposits or progress payments
rules.verbatim_quote: Diversion of funds or property received for prosecution or completion of a specific construction project or operation, or for a specified purpose in the prosecution or completion of any construction project or operation, or failure substantially to account for the application or use of such funds or property on the construction project or operation
rules.notes: Job-cost accounting by project supports compliance.

rules.title: Pay subcontractors within 7 days of receiving a progress payment
rules.plain_english: A prime contractor or subcontractor must pay each subcontractor its share of a progress payment within 7 days after receiving that progress payment, unless otherwise agreed in writing. This applies on all private works and on public works except where Public Contract Code 10262 applies.

parameters.start_event: receipt of each progress payment
parameters.amount: amounts allowed the contractor on account of the sub's work, to extent of sub's interest
parameters.scope: all private works and all public works, except where Public Contract Code 10262 applies

rules.applies_to: Prime contractors and subcontractors with lower-tier subs, private and public works
rules.verbatim_quote: A prime contractor or subcontractor shall pay to any subcontractor, not later than seven days after receipt of each progress payment, unless otherwise agreed to in writing, the respective amounts allowed the contractor on account of the work performed by the subcontractors, to the extent of each subcontractor’s interest therein.
rules.notes: Public Contract Code 10262 (state contracts) is reproduced in the Appendix, not here. Civil Code prompt-payment statutes may also apply; not covered on these pages.

rules.title: Good-faith dispute: withhold no more than 150% of disputed amount
rules.plain_english: If there is a good-faith dispute over all or part of a progress payment owed to a subcontractor, the paying contractor may withhold no more than 150% of the disputed amount and must pay the rest on time.

parameters.formula: max_withhold = 1.5 * disputed_amount; must pay = amount_due - min(amount_due, max_withhold)
parameters.condition: good faith dispute over all or any portion of progress payment

rules.applies_to: Prime contractors and subcontractors paying subs
rules.verbatim_quote: In the event that there is a good faith dispute over all or any portion of the amount due on a progress payment from the prime contractor or subcontractor to a subcontractor, the prime contractor or subcontractor may withhold no more than 150 percent of the disputed amount.
rules.notes: Formula is derived from the text.

rules.title: Late sub payment: 2% per month penalty plus attorney's fees
rules.plain_english: Violating the 7-day subcontractor payment rule is grounds for CSLB discipline and makes the contractor pay the sub a penalty of 2% of the amount due per month for every month it is unpaid. The winner of a lawsuit to collect wrongfully withheld funds gets attorney's fees and costs. These sanctions are in addition to all other remedies.

parameters.penalty_period: every month payment is not made

rules.applies_to: Prime contractors and subcontractors paying subs, private and public works
rules.verbatim_quote: Any violation of this section shall constitute a cause for disciplinary action and shall subject the licensee to a penalty, payable to the subcontractor, of 2 percent of the amount due per month for every month that payment is not made. (c) In any action for the collection of funds wrongfully withheld, the prevailing party shall be entitled to his or her attorney’s fees and costs.
rules.notes: Statute does not say whether partial months are prorated.

rules.title: Pay dump truck carriers by the 20th of the following month
rules.plain_english: A licensed contractor must pay a licensed dump truck carrier's transportation charges by the 20th day after the end of the month in which hauling was done, if the carrier submits its charges with all documentation by the 5th day after month-end, unless otherwise agreed in writing. Applies on all private and public works.

parameters.carrier_submission_deadline: 5th day following last day of calendar month in which transportation performed
parameters.payment_deadline: 20th day following last day of calendar month in which transportation performed
parameters.condition: charges and all necessary documentation submitted by the 5th day
parameters.waivable_by: written agreement between contractor and carrier
parameters.scope: all private and public works of improvement

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors using dump truck haulers (duly authorized motor carriers of property)
rules.verbatim_quote: A licensed contractor is required to pay all transportation charges submitted by a duly authorized motor carrier of property in dump truck equipment by the 20th day following the last day of the calendar month in which the transportation was performed, if the charges, including all necessary documentation, are submitted by the fifth day following the last day of the calendar month
rules.notes: Example: hauling in March, invoice by April 5, pay by April 20.

rules.title: Dump truck charges: 150% dispute withholding cap; 2% monthly penalty
rules.plain_english: In a good-faith dispute over part of a dump truck carrier's charges, the contractor may withhold up to 150% of the disputed amount (or another agreed amount).
