Late payment is grounds for discipline under B&P 7120 and carries a penalty to the carrier of 2% of the amount due per month outstanding; the winner of a collection suit gets attorney's fees and costs.

parameters.alt_withhold: amount otherwise agreed by the parties

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors using dump truck carriers
rules.verbatim_quote: In the event that there is a good faith dispute over a portion of the charges claimed, the contractor may withhold payment of up to 150 percent of the disputed amount or an amount otherwise agreed to by the parties.

rules.title: Willful departure from good and workmanlike trade standards
rules.plain_english: Willfully departing in any material way from accepted trade standards for good and workmanlike construction is grounds for discipline, unless the work followed plans and specs prepared by or under an architect.

parameters.standard: accepted trade standards for good and workmanlike construction
parameters.defense: departure was per plans and specifications prepared by or under direct supervision of an architect

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors
rules.verbatim_quote: A willful departure in any material respect from accepted trade standards for good and workmanlike construction constitutes a cause for disciplinary action, unless the departure was in accordance with plans and specifications prepared by or under the direct supervision of an architect.
rules.notes: Latent structural defects under 7109(a) have a 10-year complaint window (7091(b)).

rules.title: Deviating from plans/specs without owner consent
rules.plain_english: Willfully departing from or disregarding plans or specifications in a material way that harms someone, without the consent of the owner (or authorized representative) and of the person entitled to have the project built to those plans, is grounds for discipline. Get written change orders.

consent_needed_from: person entitled to have project completed per plans/specs

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors
rules.verbatim_quote: A willful departure from or disregard of plans or specifications in any material respect, which is prejudicial to another, without the consent of the owner or his or her duly authorized representative and without the consent of the person entitled to have the particular construction project or operation completed in accordance with such plans or specifications
rules.notes: A change-order tool can require owner sign-off before deviations from plans/specs.

rules.title: Safety violations as grounds for discipline
rules.plain_english: Violating the Title 8 safety orders in Article 12 (starting at 8 CCR 3420) is grounds for discipline whether or not anyone was hurt. Violating any Labor Code Division 5 (Cal/OSHA, Section 6300+) safety provision is grounds for discipline if it results in an employee's death or serious injury.

parameters.title8_article12_3420: discipline regardless of death or serious injury
parameters.labor_code_division5_6300: discipline if death or serious injury to an employee resulted

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors with employees
rules.verbatim_quote: Violation of any safety provision in, or authorized by, Division 5 (commencing with Section 6300) of the Labor Code resulting in death or serious injury to an employee constitutes a cause for disciplinary action.
rules.notes: The text does not name the subject of 8 CCR Article 12 (Section 3420 et seq.); it is understood to be the tree work safety orders (AB 2210), not verified on these pages. DOSH citations under that article trigger CSLB action within 18 months (7110.5).

rules.title: Willful violation of building, labor, safety and other listed laws
rules.plain_english: Willfully or deliberately disregarding state or local building laws, or the other listed laws, is grounds for discipline. The list covers pest control rules (B&P 8550/8556), Civil Code 1689.5-1689.15, safety, labor, workers' comp and unemployment insurance laws, the Subletting and Subcontracting Fair Practices Act, water well laws, Gov Code 4216 et seq., Penal Code 374.3, and building permit laws. Citations for 7110 violations carry the higher penalty range.

listed_laws: building laws of the state or any political subdivision
safety laws, labor laws, compensation insurance laws, Unemployment Insurance Code
Subletting and Subcontracting Fair Practices Act (Public Contract Code 4100 et seq.)
Health and Safety Code or Water Code provisions on digging, boring, drilling water wells
Government Code 4216 et seq. (Article 2, Chapter 3.1, Division 5, Title 1)
Penal Code 374.3 or substantially similar local law
any state or local law relating to issuance of building permits

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors
rules.verbatim_quote: Willful or deliberate disregard and violation of the building laws of the state, or of any political subdivision thereof, or of any of the following references to or provisions of law, constitutes a cause for disciplinary action against a licensee:
rules.notes: Topic labels not printed in the text: Civil Code 1689.5-1689.15 are the home solicitation contract cancellation rules; Gov Code 4216 et seq. is the underground utility excavation (811/DigAlert) law; Penal Code 374.3 is illegal dumping; B&P 8550/8556 are structural pest control provisions. Verify before display.

rules.title: Cannot require workers to release wage claims
rules.plain_english: Requiring or causing a worker to sign a release of a wage claim in violation of Labor Code 206.5 is grounds for CSLB discipline.

parameters.prohibited_act: requiring or causing execution of release of claim in violation of Labor Code 206.5

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors with employees
rules.verbatim_quote: The requiring of an execution of release of any claim or the causing of the execution of any such release in violation of Section 206.5 of the Labor Code is a cause for disciplinary action.
rules.notes: Labor Code 206.5 is in the Appendix.

rules.title: Labor Commissioner willful-violation finding or DOSH citation triggers CSLB action
rules.plain_english: When CSLB receives a certified Labor Commissioner finding of a willful or deliberate Labor Code violation (Labor Code 98.9), or DOSH citations under 8 CCR Article 12 (Section 3420 et seq.), the Registrar must start disciplinary action within 18 months of receipt.

triggers: certified copy of Labor Commissioner finding of willful/deliberate Labor Code violation (Labor Code 98.9)
DOSH citations or actions under 8 CCR Article 12 (Section 3420 et seq.)
parameters.start_event: registrar's receipt of the violation

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors with employees
rules.verbatim_quote: the registrar shall initiate disciplinary action against the licensee within 18 months from the date of the registrar’s receipt of the violation.
rules.notes: Labor violations carry license consequences, not just Labor Commissioner penalties.

rules.title: Keep all contract and financial records for 5 years after completion
rules.plain_english: A contractor must make and keep records of all contracts, documents, receipts and disbursements for its contracting work, and keep them available for CSLB inspection for at least 5 years after each project is completed. Refusing a written CSLB request to inspect them is grounds for discipline.

parameters.start_event: completion of the construction project or operation to which the records refer
violation_triggers: failure to have records available for inspection
refusal to comply with registrar's written request

rules.applies_to: All licensed contractors
rules.verbatim_quote: Failure to make and keep records showing all contracts, documents, records, receipts, and disbursements by a licensee of all of his or her transactions as a contractor, and failure to have those records available for inspection by the registrar or his or her duly authorized representative for a period of not less than five years after completion of any construction project
rules.notes: Calculation: retain_until = project_completion_date + 5 years (per project).

rules.title: Respond to CSLB written requests for records and cooperation
rules.plain_english: Delaying, obstructing or refusing, without lawful excuse, a written CSLB request for information or records, or failing to respond to a written request to cooperate in a complaint investigation, is grounds for discipline.

parameters.trigger: written request of registrar or designee
prohibited: refuse to provide information or records
fail to respond to request to cooperate in complaint investigation

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors, applicants and HIS registrants
rules.verbatim_quote: The failure of, or refusal by, a licensee to respond to a written request of the registrar to cooperate in the investigation of a complaint against that licensee constitutes a cause for disciplinary action.
rules.notes: No specific response deadline is stated in the statute; follow the date in CSLB's letter.

rules.title: False or omitted facts on license applications
rules.plain_english: Omitting or misrepresenting a material fact when obtaining or renewing a license, or when adding a classification, is grounds for discipline. Any classification added through misrepresentation is expunged from the license record on a final order.
rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors and applicants
rules.verbatim_quote: Omission or misrepresentation of a material fact by an applicant or a licensee in obtaining, or renewing a license, or in adding a classification to an existing license constitutes a cause for disciplinary action.

rules.title: Failing to complete for the contract price
rules.plain_english: Failing in a material way to complete a project for the price stated in the contract or any modification of it is grounds for discipline. Price changes need written change orders.

parameters.price_basis: price stated in contract or any modification of contract

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors
rules.verbatim_quote: Failure in a material respect on the part of a licensee to complete any construction project or operation for the price stated in the contract for such construction project or operation or in any modification of such contract constitutes a cause for disciplinary action.
rules.notes: A budget tool can flag projected cost to owner exceeding contract price plus approved change orders.

rules.title: Settling contractor debts for less than full (non-bankruptcy)
rules.plain_english: Avoiding or settling lawful contracting debts for less than the full amount through a creditor composition or reorganization under state law or agreement, receivership, assignment for the benefit of creditors, trusteeship or dissolution is grounds for discipline. Individual settlements with one creditor are not covered, and federal bankruptcy discharge is not grounds as long as non-discharged debts are paid.

covered_methods: composition, arrangement, or reorganization with creditors under state law
composition, arrangement, or reorganization by agreement
excluded: individual settlement with one creditor not part of a multi-creditor settlement
federal bankruptcy discharge, if non-discharged obligations are satisfied

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors in financial distress
rules.verbatim_quote: The avoidance or settlement by a licensee for less than the full amount of the lawful obligations of the licensee incurred as a contractor, whether by (a) composition, arrangement, or reorganization with creditors under state law, (b) composition, arrangement, or reorganization with creditors under any agreement or understanding,

rules.title: Aiding unlicensed contractors or letting them use your license
rules.plain_english: Helping an unlicensed person evade the License Law, conspiring with them, letting them use your license, or acting as their agent, partner or associate to evade the law is grounds for discipline. CSLB can order the licensee to pay injured parties, including for harm caused by the unlicensed person. Citations carry the higher penalty range.

prohibited_acts: aiding or abetting unlicensed person to evade chapter
combining or conspiring with unlicensed person
allowing license to be used by unlicensed person
acting as agent, partner, associate of unlicensed person with intent to evade
parameters.remedy: order to pay specified sum to injured party, including injury from unlicensed person's acts

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors
rules.verbatim_quote: Aiding or abetting an unlicensed person to evade the provisions of this chapter or combining or conspiring with an unlicensed person, or allowing one’s license to be used by an unlicensed person, or acting as agent or partner or associate, or otherwise, of an unlicensed person with the intent to evade the provisions of this chapter constitutes a cause for disciplinary action.

rules.title: Signing a false experience certificate for an applicant
rules.plain_english: A licensee who signs a falsified certificate of an applicant's experience, or otherwise certifies false or misleading experience claims for a license application, is subject to discipline.

parameters.prohibited_act: signing falsified experience certificate or certifying false/misleading experience claims

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors who verify employees' or others' experience
rules.verbatim_quote: Any licensee whose signature appears on a falsified certificate in support of an examinee’s experience qualifications, or otherwise certifying to false or misleading experience claims by an applicant, which have been submitted to obtain a contractor’s license shall be subject to disciplinary action.

rules.title: Misuse of a license (B&P 119) subject to CSLB remedies
rules.plain_english: Anyone, licensed or not, who commits an act prohibited by B&P 119 (misuse of licenses) is subject to CSLB administrative remedies, in addition to any civil or criminal remedies.
rules.applies_to: Licensed and unlicensed persons
rules.verbatim_quote: Any licensed or unlicensed person who commits any act prohibited by Section 119 is subject to the administrative remedies authorized by this chapter.
rules.notes: The acts prohibited by B&P 119 are not listed on these pages.

rules.title: Material failure to comply with License Law, CSLB rules, or PCC 7106
rules.plain_english: Failing in any material respect to comply with the Contractors State License Law, any CSLB rule or regulation, or Public Contract Code 7106 is grounds for discipline.

covered: Contractors State License Law (B&P 7000 et seq.)

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors (PCC 7106 relevant to public works bidders)
rules.verbatim_quote: Failure in any material respect to comply with the provisions of this chapter, or any rule or regulation adopted pursuant to this chapter, or to comply with the provisions of Section 7106 of the Public Contract Code, constitutes a cause for disciplinary action.
rules.notes: PCC 7106 content (understood to be the public works bid noncollusion declaration) is not printed here; verify.

rules.title: Willful or fraudulent act that substantially injures another
rules.plain_english: Any willful or fraudulent act by a contractor that substantially injures another person is grounds for discipline, and fixing the problem later does not by itself avoid discipline (B&P 7090.5).
rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors
rules.verbatim_quote: The doing of any wilful or fraudulent act by the licensee as a contractor in consequence of which another is substantially injured constitutes a cause for disciplinary action.

rules.title: Obstructing investigations, threatening witnesses, retaliatory firing
rules.plain_english: It is grounds for discipline to subvert or try to subvert a CSLB investigation, to threaten or harass anyone for providing evidence in a disciplinary action, arbitration or other legal action, or to fire an employee mainly because the employee tried to comply with or help enforce the License Law.

prohibited_acts: conduct that subverts or attempts to subvert a board investigation
threaten or harass any person for providing evidence in disciplinary action, arbitration, or other legal action
discharge employee primarily because of employee's attempt to comply with or aid compliance with the chapter

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors
rules.verbatim_quote: Threaten or harass any person or licensee for providing evidence in any possible or actual disciplinary action, arbitration, or other legal action. (c) Discharge an employee primarily because of the employee’s attempt to comply with or aid in compliance with the provisions of this chapter.

rules.title: Contract only in the exact licensed name and with listed personnel
rules.plain_english: A contractor must act only under the name shown on the license and with the personnel listed with CSLB (as updated through proper filings). Contracting under another name or with unreported personnel changes is grounds for discipline.

parameters.name_must_match: name of licensee as set forth upon the license
parameters.personnel_must_match: personnel as set forth in application or as later changed per chapter

rules.applies_to: All licensed contractors; contracts, bids, invoices and ads
rules.verbatim_quote: Acting in the capacity of a contractor under any license issued hereunder except: (a) in the name of the licensee as set forth upon the license, or (b) in accordance with the personnel of the licensee as set forth in the application for such license, or as later changed as provided in this chapter, constitutes a cause for disciplinary action.
rules.notes: A contract generator should print the business name exactly as on the CSLB license record. Business name change fee: see fees-misc.

rules.title: No contracting on an inactive, suspended or expired license
rules.plain_english: Acting as a contractor while your license is inactive, suspended for any reason, or expired (if still renewable under B&P 7141) is grounds for discipline, in addition to any civil or criminal remedies.

prohibited_license_statuses: expired and subject to renewal under B&P 7141

rules.applies_to: All licensed contractors; owners/GCs checking a sub's license status
rules.verbatim_quote: Acting in the capacity of a contractor under any license that has been suspended for any reason constitutes a cause for disciplinary action. (c) Acting in the capacity of a contractor under any license that has expired constitutes a cause for disciplinary action if the license is subject to renewal pursuant to Section 7141.
rules.notes: Workers' comp lapse causes automatic suspension (7125.2), which then bars contracting.

rules.title: Work only in the classifications you hold
rules.plain_english: Contracting in a classification you do not currently hold is grounds for discipline. Check the license classifications against the scope of each contract.

parameters.rule: contract scope must fall within classification(s) currently held by licensee

rules.applies_to: All licensed contractors; GCs/owners vetting subs
rules.verbatim_quote: Acting in the capacity of a contractor in a classification other than that currently held by the licensee constitutes a cause for disciplinary action.
rules.notes: Classification scopes are defined in B&P 7055-7059 and 16 CCR 832 (other chunks).

rules.title: Do not contract with an unlicensed contractor
rules.plain_english: A licensee who enters into a contract with a contractor who is not licensed can be disciplined, and the citation penalty range is the higher one ($1,500-$30,000 from July 1, 2026). Verify every subcontractor's license before signing.

parameters.prohibited_act: entering into contract with contractor not licensed
parameters.check_timing: at contract execution (and while contract in force)

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors hiring subcontractors
rules.verbatim_quote: Entering into a contract with a contractor while such contractor is not licensed as provided in this chapter constitutes a cause for disciplinary action.
rules.notes: Strong candidate for an automated CSLB license lookup at sub onboarding.

verification.checked_against: 2026 CSLB Law Book (sources/lawbook.txt), PDF page 356 (B&P 7118; B&P 7099.2)

rules.title: Asbestos inspectors must disclose ties to the abatement company
rules.plain_english: If a contractor inspects for asbestos knowing the report is required by a lender or by a public agency for a permit, it must disclose orally and in writing any ownership, common ownership, or financial relationship (including commissions or referral fees) with a company that does the corrective work. Violation is grounds for discipline and a misdemeanor fined $3,000-$5,000 and/or up to 1 year in county jail.

parameters.trigger: asbestos inspection report required by lender as loan condition or by public entity as permit condition
disclose: any financial relationship incl. commissions or referral fees with corrective-work entity
parameters.exception: contractor doing corrective work after another company's report may inspect before and after its own work

rules.applies_to: Contractors performing asbestos inspections
rules.verbatim_quote: the contractor shall disclose orally and in writing if it is owned or has any common ownership, or any financial relationship whatsoever, including, but not limited to, commissions or referral fees, with an entity in the business of performing the corrective work.
rules.notes: Asbestos is defined by Labor Code 6501.7.

rules.title: Hiring an uncertified asbestos contractor: $1,000-$3,000, then $3,000-$5,000
rules.plain_english: A contractor who knowingly, negligently, or by failing to ask contracts with someone who must be asbestos-certified (B&P 7058.5) but is not faces: first offense, an infraction with a $1,000-$3,000 fine and possible license suspension or revocation; later offenses, a misdemeanor with mandatory suspension or revocation and a $3,000-$5,000 fine and/or up to 1 year in jail.

parameters.required_certification: B&P 7058.5 asbestos certification (asbestos-related work per Labor Code 6501.8)

rules.applies_to: Contractors, applicants and persons required to be licensed who hire asbestos subcontractors
rules.verbatim_quote: Any contractor, applicant for licensure, or person required to be licensed, who, either knowingly or negligently, or by reason of a failure to inquire, enters into a contract with another person who is required to be, and is not, certified pursuant to Section 7058.5 to engage in asbestos-related work, as defined in Section 6501.8 of the Labor Code, is subject to the following penalties:
rules.notes: Failure to inquire is enough: verify certification before contracting.

rules.title: Hiring an uncertified hazardous substance removal contractor
rules.plain_english: A contractor who knowingly, negligently, or by failing to ask contracts with someone who must hold hazardous substance removal/remedial action certification (B&P 7058.7) but does not faces the same penalties: first offense $1,000-$3,000 infraction; subsequent offenses a misdemeanor with mandatory license suspension or revocation and $3,000-$5,000 fine and/or up to 1 year in jail.

parameters.required_certification: B&P 7058.7 hazardous substance removal or remedial action certification

rules.applies_to: Contractors hiring hazardous substance removal subcontractors
rules.verbatim_quote: Any contractor who, either knowingly or negligently, or by reason of a failure to inquire, enters into a contract with another person who is required to be, and is not certified pursuant to Section 7058.7 to engage in a removal or remedial action, as defined in Section 7058.7, is subject to the following penalties:

rules.title: Failing to work on the project with reasonable diligence
rules.plain_english: Willfully failing or refusing, without legal excuse, to carry out a project with reasonable diligence, causing material injury to someone, is grounds for discipline.
rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors
rules.verbatim_quote: Wilful failure or refusal without legal excuse on the part of a licensee as a contractor to prosecute a construction project or operation with reasonable diligence causing material injury to another constitutes a cause for disciplinary action.
rules.notes: Schedule tracking with documented delay causes supports a legal-excuse defense.

rules.title: Not paying suppliers/vendors when able or when paid for that work
rules.plain_english: Willfully failing to pay for materials or services when due, if the contractor can pay or has received enough money for that job, is grounds for discipline, as is falsely denying a debt to get a discount or to hinder, delay or defraud the creditor.

triggers: has received sufficient funds for the particular project
parameters.also_prohibited: false denial of amount due or validity of claim, to obtain discount or to hinder, delay, or defraud

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors and their officers/agents
rules.verbatim_quote: Wilful or deliberate failure by any licensee or agent or officer thereof to pay any moneys, when due for any materials or services rendered in connection with his operations as a contractor, when he has the capacity to pay or when he has received sufficient funds therefor as payment for the particular construction work, project, or operation
rules.notes: A pay-when-paid tracker can flag supplier invoices unpaid after owner payment for that job is received.

rules.title: People tied to denied, revoked or suspended licenses cannot be personnel of record
rules.plain_english: A person denied a license (other than for lacking experience for a supplemental class), whose license was revoked or is suspended, or who was a partner, officer, director, manager or associate of such a company and knew of or took part in the violations, cannot be an officer, director, associate, partner, manager, qualifier or personnel of record of a licensee. Employing them in any role other than a non-supervising bona fide employee is grounds for discipline.

barred_persons: denied a license (not merely for insufficient experience for a supplemental classification)
failed to renew while under suspension
partner/officer/director/manager/associate of such an entity who knew of or participated in the prohibited acts

rules.applies_to: Contracting companies hiring or appointing officers, managers or qualifiers
rules.verbatim_quote: shall be prohibited from serving as an officer, director, associate, partner, manager, qualifying individual, or member of the personnel of record of a licensee, and the employment, election, or association of this type of person by a licensee in any capacity other than as a nonsupervising bona fide employee shall constitute grounds for disciplinary action.
rules.notes: Screen proposed officers/qualifiers against CSLB records before appointment.

rules.title: Leaving the company does not relieve officers or qualifiers of a citation
rules.plain_english: A partner, officer, director, manager or associate who knew of or participated in the cited acts stays responsible for complying with the citation after leaving the company, and the 7121 bar applies if it is not complied with. A qualifying individual who leaves after the act stays responsible regardless of knowledge, and the 7122.5 rule applies.

parameters.officers_partners: responsible if they had knowledge of or participated in the cited acts (B&P 7121.1)
parameters.qualifying_individual: responsible regardless of knowledge if disassociated after the act (B&P 7122.1)

rules.applies_to: Officers, partners, managers and qualifiers of cited licensees
rules.verbatim_quote: the disassociation of a partner, officer, director, manager, or associate from the license of a partnership, corporation, limited liability company, firm, or association whose license has been cited pursuant to Section 7099 shall not relieve the partner, officer, director, manager, or associate from responsibility for complying with the citation

verification.checked_against: 2026 CSLB Law Book (sources/lawbook.txt), PDF pages 359, 361-362 (B&P 7121.1; B&P 7122.1)

rules.title: Qualifier of a revoked or suspended license is barred regardless of knowledge
rules.plain_english: Anyone who was the qualifying individual on a license that was revoked, is suspended, or was not renewed while suspended cannot be an officer, director, associate, partner, manager or qualifier of a licensee, even without knowledge of the violations. Employing or associating with them in those roles is grounds for discipline.

parameters.barred_person: qualifying individual on revoked, suspended, or not-renewed-while-suspended license

rules.applies_to: Contracting companies appointing qualifiers (RMO/RME) or officers
rules.verbatim_quote: A person who was the qualifying individual on a revoked license, or of a license under suspension, or of a license that was not renewed while it was under suspension, shall be prohibited from serving as an officer, director, associate, partner, manager, or qualifying individual of a licensee, whether or not the individual had knowledge of or participated in the prohibited acts or omissions

rules.title: Revoked-license principals may only work as non-supervising employees
rules.plain_english: An officer, owner, manager, partner or associate of a revoked license who knew of or took part in the violations, or the qualifier of a revoked license (regardless of knowledge), who is not yet eligible for reinstatement under B&P 7102, may not do any licensed contracting act for a licensee except as a bona fide non-supervising employee. Violation is a misdemeanor: fine of at least $4,500 and/or 90 days to 1 year in county jail; charges may be filed within 4 years.

restricted_persons: listed officer/director/owner/manager/partner/associate of revoked license who knew of or participated in the acts
qualifier of revoked license during the acts, regardless of knowledge
parameters.condition: not eligible for reinstatement under B&P 7102

rules.applies_to: Individuals tied to revoked licenses
rules.verbatim_quote: A violation of this section is a misdemeanor punishable by a fine of not less than four thousand five hundred dollars ($4,500), by imprisonment in a county jail for not less than 90 days nor more than one year, or by both the fine and imprisonment.

rules.title: Revoked-license individuals must tell prospective employers in writing
rules.plain_english: Before taking any job with a licensed contracting business, a person described in B&P 7121.6(a) or (b) must give the prospective employer written notice of the license revocation.

parameters.timing: prior to becoming employed in any capacity

rules.applies_to: Individuals tied to revoked licenses; contractors hiring them
rules.verbatim_quote: Prior to becoming employed in any capacity by an entity that is subject to licensure under this chapter, an individual who is described in subdivision (a) or (b) of Section 7121.6 shall provide the prospective employer with written notice of the license revocation.
rules.notes: Onboarding checklists can ask for and file this notice.

rules.title: Knowingly employing a revoked-license individual in a supervising role
rules.plain_english: A qualifier, officer, partner or other person named on a license may not knowingly employ a person described in B&P 7121.6(a) or (b) except as a bona fide non-supervising employee. Violation is a misdemeanor: fine of at least $4,500 and/or 30 days to 1 year in county jail; charges may be filed within 4 years.
rules.applies_to: Contracting companies and their named personnel
rules.verbatim_quote: A qualifying individual, officer, partner, or other person named on a license shall not knowingly employ an individual who is described in subdivision (a) or (b) of Section 7121.6, except as a bona fide nonsupervising employee.

rules.title: Definition: bona fide nonsupervising employee
rules.plain_english: A bona fide non-supervising employee is someone exempt from licensing as an employee under B&P 7053 who does not meet the independent-contractor test of Labor Code 2750.5.
rules.applies_to: Contracting companies employing barred individuals
rules.verbatim_quote: “bona fide nonsupervising employee” means a person who is exempt from the provisions of this chapter under Section 7053, and who does not otherwise meet the test of an independent contractor, as set forth under Section 2750.5 of the Labor Code.

rules.title: Officers and partners can be disciplined for the company's violations they knew of
rules.plain_english: A violation by a business is also grounds for discipline against any of its partners, officers, directors, managers or associates who hold their own license, if they were in that role at the time and knew of or participated in the violation.

parameters.timing: in that role when act occurred

rules.applies_to: Officers and partners of contracting businesses who hold licenses
rules.verbatim_quote: a licensee other than the individual qualifying on behalf of the individual or entity, if the licensee was a partner, officer, director, manager, or associate of that individual, partnership, corporation, limited liability company, firm, or association at the time the act or omission occurred, and had knowledge of or participated in the prohibited act or omission.

rules.title: Qualifiers are liable for the company's violations even without knowledge
rules.plain_english: A violation by a business is grounds for discipline against whoever was its qualifying individual at the time, whether or not the qualifier knew of or participated in it. A qualifier who leaves also stays responsible for arbitration awards arising from their time as qualifier.

parameters.who: qualifying individual at the time of the act

rules.applies_to: RMOs, RMEs and other qualifying individuals
rules.verbatim_quote: likewise constitutes a cause for disciplinary action against a licensee who at the time that the act or omission occurred was the qualifying individual of that individual, partnership, corporation, limited liability company, firm, or association, whether or not he or she had knowledge of or participated in the prohibited act or omission.
rules.notes: Qualifiers should monitor citations, arbitrations and complaints against every license they qualify.

verification.checked_against: 2026 CSLB Law Book (sources/lawbook.txt), PDF page 362 (B&P 7122.5; B&P 7122.2)

rules.title: Departing qualifier still responsible for arbitration awards
rules.plain_english: A qualifying individual who disassociates from a license referred to CSLB arbitration remains responsible for complying with any award arising from acts or omissions while they were qualifier, and B&P 7122.5 applies if the licensee does not comply.

parameters.responsible_for: arbitration award for acts/omissions committed while acting as qualifier

rules.applies_to: RMOs, RMEs and other qualifying individuals
rules.verbatim_quote: the disassociation of a qualifying individual from a license that has been referred to arbitration pursuant to Section 7085 shall not relieve the qualifying individual from the responsibility of complying with an arbitration award rendered as a result of acts or omissions committed while acting as the qualifying individual for the license

rules.title: Substantially related criminal conviction
rules.plain_english: A conviction for a crime substantially related to a contractor's qualifications, functions and duties is grounds for discipline; the conviction record is conclusive evidence. A guilty plea, guilty verdict, or no-contest plea followed by conviction counts, and CSLB may act once the appeal time passes, the conviction is affirmed, or probation is granted, even if the plea is later withdrawn under Penal Code 1203.4.

conviction_includes: conviction following plea of nolo contendere
board_may_act_when: order granting probation suspending imposition of sentence

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors and applicants
rules.verbatim_quote: A conviction of a crime substantially related to the qualifications, functions and duties of a contractor constitutes a cause for disciplinary action. The record of the conviction shall be conclusive evidence thereof.

verification.checked_against: 2026 CSLB Law Book (sources/lawbook.txt), PDF pages 362-363 (B&P 7123; B&P 7124)

rules.title: Post-disaster price gouging conviction: at least 6-month suspension
rules.plain_english: If a contractor is convicted of price gouging after a declared emergency (Penal Code 396 or similar local law) in selling repair or reconstruction services, CSLB must discipline, including at least a 6-month suspension or permanent revocation.

parameters.trigger: conviction under Penal Code 396 or substantially similar local ordinance re repair or reconstruction services

rules.applies_to: Contractors doing post-disaster repair or reconstruction
rules.verbatim_quote: the Contractors State License Board shall take disciplinary action against the contractor, which shall include a suspension of at least six months or the permanent revocation of the contractor’s license.
rules.notes: Penal Code 396 price limits are in the Appendix, not on these pages.

rules.title: Which complaints CSLB discloses to the public
rules.plain_english: CSLB publicly discloses the date, nature and status of complaints that have been referred for accusation, or referred for investigation after staff found a probable violation (supervisor-reviewed) serious enough for suspension, revocation or criminal prosecution. Each disclosure carries a disclaimer that it is only an allegation. Complaints resolved in the contractor's favor are not disclosed.

disclosed_complaints: referred for investigation after probable-violation determination, supervisor-reviewed, alleging risk of harm warranting suspension/revocation or criminal prosecution

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors; owners researching contractors
rules.verbatim_quote: The registrar shall make available to members of the public the date, nature, and status of all complaints on file against a licensee that do either of the following: (1) Have been referred for accusation.
rules.notes: Last amended Stats 2022 ch 293 (AB 2916); effective date not printed.

rules.title: Letters of admonishment are public for 1 or 2 years
rules.plain_english: A letter of admonishment is not treated as resolved in the contractor's favor and is publicly disclosed for 1 or 2 years from the date of service, based on the gravity, good faith and prior-violation factors.

parameters.start_event: date of service of letter of admonishment (B&P 7099.9(c))

rules.applies_to: Licensees issued letters of admonishment; owners researching contractors
rules.verbatim_quote: A letter of admonishment issued to a licensee shall be disclosed for a period of either one year or two years from the date of service described in subdivision (c) of Section 7099.9.

rules.title: Citations are public until 5 years after compliance
rules.plain_english: Citations are disclosed from issuance until 5 years after the date of compliance, if no other disciplinary action is filed in that period; otherwise all actions stay disclosed as long as the most recent one is. The disclosure also appears on any other license that shares a qualifier listed on the cited license.

parameters.extension_rule: if additional disciplinary action filed during 5 years, all disclosed as long as most recent action is disclosable
parameters.cross_posting: also on license record of any other license with a qualifier who is personnel of record of the cited license, for the same period

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors; owners/GCs vetting contractors
rules.verbatim_quote: Citations shall be disclosed from the date of issuance and for five years after the date of compliance if no additional disciplinary actions have been filed against the licensee during the five-year period.
rules.notes: Calculation: citation_public_until = compliance_date + 5 years (absent new actions).

rules.title: Accusations public for 7 years after settlement; revocations forever
rules.plain_english: Accusations that result in suspension, stayed suspension or stayed revocation are disclosed from filing until 7 years after settlement (including probation terms), if no new actions are filed; otherwise as long as the latest action is disclosable. Revocations that are not stayed are disclosed indefinitely.

parameters.extension_rule: if additional disciplinary action filed during 7 years, all disclosed as long as most recent is disclosable
parameters.unstayed_revocation_disclosure: indefinite from effective date of revocation

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors; owners/GCs vetting contractors
rules.verbatim_quote: Accusations that result in suspension, stayed suspension, or stayed revocation of the contractor’s license shall be disclosed from the date the accusation is filed and for seven years after the accusation has been settled, including the terms and conditions of probation if no additional disciplinary actions have been filed against the licensee during the seven-year period.

rules.title: Workers' comp certificate must be on file with CSLB at all times
rules.plain_english: To get, reinstate, reactivate, renew or keep a license, the contractor must always have on file with CSLB a current Certificate of Workers' Compensation Insurance (filed by a California-licensed insurer) or a Certification of Self-Insurance (from the Director of Industrial Relations), in the license's business name, unless an exemption applies. Willful violation of workers' comp laws is grounds for discipline.

documents_accepted: Certificate of Workers' Compensation Insurance (filed by insurer licensed in CA)
Certification of Self-Insurance (issued by Director of Industrial Relations)

rules.applies_to: All active licensees and applicants, unless exempt
rules.verbatim_quote: the board shall require as a condition precedent to the issuance, reinstatement, reactivation, renewal, or continued maintenance of a license, that the applicant or licensee have on file at all times a current and valid Certificate of Workers’ Compensation Insurance or Certification of Self-Insurance in the applicant’s or licensee’s business name.
rules.notes: Same core requirement continues in the version operative January 1, 2028, with a much narrower exemption.

rules.title: Workers' comp exemption (through 2027): no employees and not C-8/C-20/C-22/C-39/D-49
rules.plain_english: Until January 1, 2028, a licensee may skip workers' comp only if it has no employees, files CSLB's exemption statement certifying that, and does not hold a C-8, C-20, C-22, C-39 or D-49 classification. A joint venture with no employees that files the statement is also exempt.

exemption_conditions_all_required: no employees subject to CA workers' comp law
exemption statement filed on CSLB form before issuance/reinstatement/reactivation/continued maintenance
does not hold C-8, C-20, C-22, C-39, or D-49 (C-61 subcategory) classification
parameters.joint_venture_exemption: JV under B&P 7029 with no employees that files the statement

rules.applies_to: Sole owners and entities with no employees
rules.verbatim_quote: Has no employees provided that the applicant or licensee files a statement with the board on a form prescribed by the registrar before the issuance, reinstatement, reactivation, or continued maintenance of a license, certifying that the applicant or licensee does not employ any person in any manner so as to become subject to the workers’ compensation laws of California
rules.notes: Class names checked against 16 CCR 832.08/.20/.22/.39/.61 in the book: C-8 Concrete, C-20 Warm-Air Heating, Ventilating and Air-Conditioning, C-22 Asbestos Abatement, C-39 Roofing, D-49 Tree Service (a C-61 subcategory).

verification.checked_against: 2026 CSLB Law Book (sources/lawbook.txt), PDF pages 365-366 (B&P 7125(b)-(c), version repealed January 1, 2028); 16 CCR 832.08-832.61 class definitions
verification.correction: No error. Both exemption conditions, the five excluded classifications, the joint-venture exemption and the 2028 repeal date confirmed. Replaced the "verify before display" note with the class names as checked in 16 CCR 832.

rules.title: No workers' comp certificate needed while license is inactive
rules.plain_english: A license that is inactive on CSLB's records does not need a workers' comp certificate, self-insurance certificate or exemption while inactive.
rules.applies_to: Holders of inactive licenses
rules.verbatim_quote: A Certificate of Workers’ Compensation Insurance, Certification of Self-Insurance, or exemption certificate is not required of a holder of a license that has been inactivated on the official records of the board during the period the license is inactive.
rules.notes: Contracting on an inactive license is itself grounds for discipline (7117.5).

verification.checked_against: 2026 CSLB Law Book (sources/lawbook.txt), PDF pages 366, 368 (B&P 7125(d) [until Jan 1, 2028]; B&P 7125(c) [from Jan 1, 2028])

rules.title: C-39 classification removed if no workers' comp certificate
rules.plain_english: For a multi-class license that includes C-39 (and was active on January 1, 2013), CSLB removes the C-39 classification instead of suspending the whole license if no valid workers' comp or self-insurance certificate is on file. If such a licensee is later found to have employees and no certificate, the license is automatically suspended.

parameters.condition: active license including C-39 plus other classification(s), no valid WC/self-insurance certificate
parameters.action: remove C-39 classification in lieu of automatic suspension

rules.applies_to: Licensees holding C-39 with other classifications
rules.verbatim_quote: the registrar shall, in lieu of the automatic license suspension otherwise required under this article, remove the C-39 classification from the license unless a valid Certificate of Workers’ Compensation Insurance or Certification of Self-Insurance is received by the registrar.

rules.title: C-8, C-20, C-22 or D-49 classification removed if no workers' comp certificate
rules.plain_english: For a license active after July 1, 2023 that includes C-8, C-20, C-22 or D-49 plus another classification, CSLB removes those classifications instead of suspending the license if no valid workers' comp or self-insurance certificate is on file. If the licensee is later found to have employees and no certificate, the license is automatically suspended.

parameters.condition: active license after July 1, 2023 including one of these plus other classification(s); no valid WC/self-insurance certificate
parameters.action: remove those classifications in lieu of automatic suspension

rules.applies_to: Licensees holding C-8, C-20, C-22 or D-49 with other classifications
rules.verbatim_quote: For any licensee whose license, after July 1, 2023, is active and includes a C-8, C-20, C-22, or D-49 classification, in addition to any other classification, the registrar shall, in lieu of the automatic license suspension otherwise required under this article, remove the C-8, C-20, C-22, or D-49 classification from the license

rules.title: From January 1, 2028: workers' comp required for all active licensees
rules.plain_english: Starting January 1, 2028, the no-employee exemption ends for individual and entity licensees: every active licensee must have a workers' comp or self-insurance certificate on file. The only exemption is a joint venture with no employees that files CSLB's statement. Inactive licenses still need no certificate.

parameters.only_exemption: joint venture under B&P 7029 with no employees that files CSLB statement

rules.applies_to: All active licensees, including sole owners with no employees, from January 1, 2028
rules.verbatim_quote: This section does not apply to an applicant or licensee organized as a joint venture pursuant to Section 7029 that has no employees, provided that the applicant or licensee files a statement with the board on a form prescribed by the registrar before the issuance, reinstatement, reactivation, or continued maintenance of a license
rules.notes: Major upcoming change (SB 216 / SB 1455). Sole proprietors relying on the exemption need coverage in place by January 1, 2028 or face automatic suspension under 7125.2. A later statute could change this date; re-check before 2028.

rules.title: Workers' comp certificate accepted retroactively if received within 90 days
rules.plain_english: CSLB accepts a workers' comp certificate as of its effective date, and reinstates the license retroactive to that date, if CSLB receives it within 90 days after the effective date. Later filings can still be retroactive if the licensee shows the gap was beyond its control. During that acceptance period the contractor is considered duly licensed.

parameters.start_event: effective date shown on the certificate
parameters.result: accepted as of effective date; license reinstated retroactively if otherwise eligible
parameters.late_filing_exception: showing on registrar form that failure was due to circumstances beyond licensee's control

rules.applies_to: Licensees reinstating after workers' comp lapse or filing new certificates
rules.verbatim_quote: The registrar shall accept a certificate required by Section 7125 as of the effective date shown on the certificate, if the certificate is received by the registrar within 90 days after that date, and shall reinstate the license to which the certificate pertains, if otherwise eligible, retroactive to the effective date of the certificate.
rules.notes: Calculation: filing_deadline_for_retroactivity = certificate_effective_date + 90 days. Relevant to whether work during a gap was licensed (B&P 7031 payment rights, earlier chunk).

verification.checked_against: 2026 CSLB Law Book (sources/lawbook.txt), PDF pages 368-370 (B&P 7125.1; B&P 7125.3)

rules.title: Workers' comp lapse = automatic license suspension on the lapse date
rules.plain_english: If a licensee required to carry workers' comp fails to get or keep it, the license is automatically suspended as of the earlier of the date coverage lapses or the date coverage was first required. Reinstatement is by filing proof of coverage (B&P 7125 and 7125.1). The suspension does not change the licensee's status as an employer under Labor Code 3716.

parameters.trigger: failure to obtain or maintain required workers' comp coverage
parameters.suspension_effective: earlier of (coverage lapse date) or (date coverage required to be obtained)
parameters.reinstatement: any time, by proof of compliance under B&P 7125 and 7125.1
parameters.unlicensed_person_citation: B&P 7028.7 citation; 7125.2(d) says a hearing under 7028.10 is granted if requested within 15 working days after service, but B&P 7099.8(a) ("notwithstanding any other law") requires a written hearing request within 15 days after service of a 7028.7 citation. Safe deadline: 15 calendar days.

rules.applies_to: All licensees required to carry workers' comp
rules.verbatim_quote: The license suspension imposed by this section is effective upon the earlier of either of the following: (1) On the date that the relevant workers’ compensation insurance coverage lapses. (2) On the date that workers’ compensation coverage is required to be obtained.
rules.notes: Insurers report cancellations to CSLB (7125(e)). A policy-renewal tracker should alert well before the policy expiration date. For unlicensed persons cited under 7028.7, calendar the hearing request at 15 calendar days after service (7099.8(a), PDF page 342), not 15 working days.

rules.title: CSLB notice of workers' comp suspension; pending posting up to 45 days
rules.plain_english: When a license is suspended for a workers' comp lapse, CSLB's notice must give the reason and effective date, state that a pending suspension will be posted on the public license record for up to 45 days before the suspension periods are posted, and explain how to reinstate.

notice_contents: reason for suspension and effective date
statement that pending suspension posted to license record for not more than 45 days before suspension periods posted

rules.applies_to: Licensees suspended for workers' comp lapse
rules.verbatim_quote: A statement informing the licensee that a pending suspension will be posted to the license record for not more than 45 days prior to the posting of any license suspension periods required under this article.
rules.notes: Owners/GCs checking a sub's license should look for a posted pending WC suspension.

rules.title: False workers' comp exemption, or hiring before filing a certificate
rules.plain_english: Filing a false workers' comp exemption, hiring an employee after filing an exemption without first filing a workers' comp or self-insurance certificate, or employing workers without coverage is grounds for discipline, including minimum civil penalties. File the certificate before the first employee starts.

prohibited_acts: employing a covered person after filing exemption without first filing WC or self-insurance certificate
employing a covered person without maintaining coverage
parameters.timing_rule: certificate must be filed BEFORE employing anyone after an exemption

rules.applies_to: Licensees with workers' comp exemptions; all employers
rules.verbatim_quote: The filing of the exemption certificate prescribed by this article that is false, or the employment of a person subject to coverage under the workers’ compensation laws after the filing of an exemption certificate without first filing a Certificate of Workers’ Compensation Insurance or Certification of Self-Insurance in accordance with the provisions of this article

rules.title: Uninsured employees: minimum $10,000 (sole owner) or $20,000 (entity) per violation
rules.plain_english: A licensee found to have employed workers without workers' comp faces a minimum civil penalty of $10,000 per violation if a sole owner, or $20,000 per violation if a partnership, corporation, LLC or tribal business. Additional penalties for later violations may be added, up to $30,000 total per occurrence.
rules.applies_to: All licensed employers
rules.verbatim_quote: A minimum civil penalty of ten thousand dollars ($10,000) per violation for any sole owner licensee found to have employed workers without maintaining workers’ compensation coverage. (2) A minimum civil penalty of twenty thousand dollars ($20,000) per violation for any partnership, corporation, limited liability company, or tribal business licensee
rules.notes: Amended by SB 291 (Stats 2025 ch 455) effective January 1, 2026. How the $30,000 cap interacts with the minimums ('not to exceed a total of $30,000 per occurrence') should be confirmed with CSLB.

rules.title: Qualifier misdemeanor for workers' comp violations; no renewal without certificate
rules.plain_english: The qualifier responsible for compliance (B&P 7068.1) is guilty of a misdemeanor for committing or failing to prevent these workers' comp violations. CSLB will not renew or reinstate the license until a current workers' comp or self-insurance certificate in the business name is provided.

parameters.qualifier_liability: misdemeanor for committing or failing to prevent the violation
parameters.renewal_reinstatement_blocked_until: current and valid WC or self-insurance certificate in business name provided

rules.applies_to: Qualifiers (RMO/RME) and licensees
rules.verbatim_quote: Any qualifier for a license who, under Section 7068.1, is responsible for assuring that a licensee complies with the provisions of this chapter is also guilty of a misdemeanor for committing or failing to prevent the commission of any of the acts that are cause for disciplinary action under this section.

rules.title: Recertify workers' comp exemption (or file certificate) at every renewal
rules.plain_english: At each renewal, an active licensee with a workers' comp exemption on file must either recertify the exemption on the renewal form or provide a current workers' comp or self-insurance certificate. Otherwise the license will not be renewed.

options: complete recertification statement on renewal form
provide current WC or self-insurance certificate

rules.applies_to: Active licensees with a workers' comp exemption on file
rules.verbatim_quote: The license shall not be renewed unless a licensee with an exemption for workers’ compensation insurance on file with the board recertifies the exemption status or provides a current and valid Certificate of Workers’ Compensation Insurance or Certificate of Self-Insurance in conjunction with the license renewal.
rules.notes: Exemptions for non-JV licensees end January 1, 2028 (7125 operative 2028).

rules.title: Fix a rejected renewal within 30 days for retroactive renewal
rules.plain_english: If a renewal is rejected because the workers' comp exemption recertification/certificate or the workers' comp class codes were missing, and CSLB receives them within 30 days after notifying you of the rejection, the renewal is made retroactive to the postmark date of the original renewal. After 30 days, no retroactive renewal under these sections.

parameters.start_event: board's notification of renewal rejection
parameters.result_if_cured: retroactive renewal under B&P 7141.5 back to postmark date of renewal
parameters.result_if_not_cured: not eligible for retroactive renewal under these subdivisions

rules.applies_to: Licensees renewing
rules.verbatim_quote: If the documentation required by subdivision (a) is not provided with the license renewal but is received within 30 days after notification by the board of the renewal rejection, the registrar shall grant a retroactive renewal pursuant to Section 7141.5 back to the date of the postmark of the otherwise acceptable renewal.
rules.effective: B&P 7125.5: effective January 1, 2012 (Stats 2011 ch 546). B&P 7125.6: effective January 1, 2024, operative July 1, 2024 (Stats 2023 ch 323, AB 336).
rules.notes: Avoids a gap in licensure if cured in time.

verification.checked_against: 2026 CSLB Law Book (sources/lawbook.txt), PDF pages 371-372 (B&P 7125.5(c); B&P 7125.6(b)(2))
verification.correction: 30-day cure period, start event (board notification of renewal rejection), retroactive renewal under 7141.5 to postmark date, and loss of retroactivity after 30 days confirmed for both 7125.5(c) and 7125.6(b)(2). rules.title: Report top 3 workers' comp class codes at renewal
rules.plain_english: At renewal, every active licensee with (or required to have) a workers' comp or self-insurance certificate must certify on the renewal form the three workers' comp classification codes with the highest estimated payroll on the policy, or all codes if fewer than three. The license will not be renewed without them, and CSLB posts the codes on the public license detail.

parameters.selection_rule: classification codes with highest estimated payroll reported on the policy
parameters.if_fewer_than_3: report every classification code on the policy
parameters.public_display: codes shown on CSLB public license detail

rules.applies_to: Active licensees with workers' comp coverage
rules.verbatim_quote: shall certify on the license renewal form for the three workers’ compensation classification codes for which the highest estimated payroll is reported on the policy. If the licensee has fewer than three classification codes reported on the policy, the licensee shall provide every classification code reported on the policy.
rules.notes: Tool can sort policy class codes by estimated payroll and output the top 3. Owners/GCs can compare posted codes to the trade being performed.

rules.title: CSLB to audit/verify no-employee exemptions by January 1, 2027
rules.plain_english: By January 1, 2027, CSLB must set up a process (including audits, proof, or other evidence) to verify that licensees claiming the no-employee workers' comp exemption are actually eligible. Exempt contractors should be ready to prove they have no employees.

parameters.target: applicants/licensees claiming exemption for having no employees

rules.applies_to: Licensees with a workers' comp exemption
rules.verbatim_quote: By no later than January 1, 2027, the board shall establish a process and procedure, which shall include an audit, proof, or other means to obtain evidence to verify that an applicant or licensee without an employee or employees is eligible for exemption from the workers’ compensation insurance requirement pursuant to Section 7125.
rules.notes: Keep records showing no employees (e.g., payroll records, subcontractor licenses/WC certificates).

rules.title: Violating workers' comp article is a misdemeanor; 2-year prosecution window
rules.plain_english: A licensee, agent or officer who violates the workers' comp reporting article (B&P 7125-7127) is guilty of a misdemeanor, and so is an unlicensed person acting as a contractor without workers' comp required by Labor Code 3700. Prosecution must start within 2 years.

who: licensee, agent, or officer violating Article 7.5
unlicensed person acting as contractor violating Labor Code 3700
parameters.start_event: commission of the offense (Penal Code 802)

rules.applies_to: Licensed and unlicensed contractors with employees
rules.verbatim_quote: Any licensee or agent or officer thereof, who violates, or omits to comply with, any of the provisions of this article is guilty of a misdemeanor. (b) Any person not licensed in accordance with this chapter who is acting as a contractor and who violates, or omits to comply with, Section 3700 of the Labor Code is guilty of a misdemeanor.
rules.notes: See also Health and Safety Code 19825 (workers' comp declaration on building permits), in Appendix.

rules.title: CSLB stop order: no employee labor until workers' comp is secured
rules.plain_english: If an employer subject to licensure (licensed or not) has no workers' comp as required by Labor Code 3700, CSLB can serve a stop order barring use of employee labor, effective immediately on service. The employer must pay affected employees for lost time, up to 10 days, while it gets into compliance.

parameters.trigger: employer subject to licensure failed to secure workers' comp (Labor Code 3700)

rules.applies_to: Contractors (licensed or unlicensed) with employees
rules.verbatim_quote: The stop order shall become effective immediately upon service. An employee affected by the work stoppage shall be paid by the employer for his or her time lost, not exceeding 10 days, pending compliance by the employer.
rules.notes: Owners/GCs should expect schedule impacts if a sub receives a stop order.

rules.title: Ignoring a stop order: up to 60 days jail and/or $10,000 fine
rules.plain_english: Any employer, officer, or person controlling a workplace or employees who does not obey a served CSLB stop order commits a misdemeanor punishable by up to 60 days in county jail, a fine up to $10,000, or both.

who: any person having direction, management, or control of place of employment or employees

rules.applies_to: Employers, officers and site supervisors
rules.verbatim_quote: Failure of any employer, officer, or any person having direction, management, or control of any place of employment or of employees to observe a stop order issued and served upon him or her pursuant to this section is a misdemeanor punishable by imprisonment in the county jail not exceeding 60 days or by a fine not exceeding ten thousand dollars ($10,000), or both.

rules.title: Protest a stop order within 20 days; hearing within 5 days
rules.plain_english: An employer can protest a stop order by filing a written hearing request with the Registrar within 20 days after service. The hearing must be held within 5 days of filing; the stop order is affirmed or dismissed at the end, written findings are served within 24 hours by registered or certified mail, and a writ of mandate to superior court must be filed within 45 days after the findings are mailed.

parameters.protest_form: written request for hearing filed with registrar

rules.applies_to: Employers served with a CSLB stop order
rules.verbatim_quote: An employer who is subject to this section may protest the stop order by making and filing with the registrar a written request for a hearing within 20 days after service of the stop order. The hearing shall be held within five days from the date of filing the request.
rules.notes: Stop order remains in effect during the protest; the text does not provide a stay.

rules.title: CSLB application fees (statutory base and caps)
rules.plain_english: CSLB application fees are set by regulation within statutory limits: original license, single class $450 (up to $563); each extra class with an original application $150 (up to $188); adding a class to an existing license $230 (up to $288); replacing the qualifier $230 (up to $288); adding non-qualifier personnel $125 (up to $157); asbestos certification $125 (up to $157); hazardous substance removal certification $125 (up to $157). Exam fees are paid at actual cost to the testing organization.

parameters.exam_fee: no greater than actual cost of administration; paid directly to the testing organization

rules.applies_to: License applicants and licensees changing classifications or personnel
rules.verbatim_quote: The application fee for an original license in a single classification shall be four hundred fifty dollars ($450) and may be increased to not more than five hundred sixty-three dollars ($563).
rules.notes: Statute gives base amounts and maximums; the fee actually charged is set by CSLB regulation (16 CCR 811) and may be anywhere up to the cap. Check the current CSLB fee schedule before quoting. Fees are nonrefundable (7138). 16 CCR 811 (PDF pages 451-452) currently sets these fees at the statutory base amounts.

verification.checked_against: 2026 CSLB Law Book (sources/lawbook.txt), PDF pages 374-375 (B&P 7137(a)(1)-(2)); 16 CCR 811 (PDF pages 451-452)
verification.correction: No error. All seven application fee base/maximum pairs and the exam-fee rule match 7137(a)(1)-(2). Added a note that 16 CCR 811(a) (PDF page 451) currently charges the base amounts.

rules.title: CSLB initial license and HIS registration fees
rules.plain_english: Initial license fee (active or inactive): individual owner $200 (up to $250); partnership, corporation, LLC or joint venture $350 (up to $438). Home improvement salesperson registration $200 (up to $250).
rules.applies_to: New licensees and HIS registrants
rules.verbatim_quote: The initial license fee for an active or inactive license for an individual owner shall be two hundred dollars ($200) and may be increased to not more than two hundred fifty dollars ($250).
rules.notes: Actual fee is set by regulation within the cap; check the current CSLB fee schedule. 16 CCR 811 (PDF pages 451-452) currently sets these fees at the statutory base amounts.

verification.checked_against: 2026 CSLB Law Book (sources/lawbook.txt), PDF page 375 (B&P 7137(a)(3)(A)-(C)); 16 CCR 811 (PDF pages 451-452)
verification.correction: No error. All three base/maximum pairs match 7137(a)(3)(A)-(C). Added a note that 16 CCR 811(c) (PDF page 451) currently charges the base amounts.

rules.title: Veterans get 50% off initial license/registration fees
rules.plain_english: CSLB must cut initial license and registration fees by 50% for applicants who are U.S. Armed Forces veterans (including National Guard or Reserve) not dishonorably discharged. Proof: a state driver's license or ID marked Veteran, or a DD214 long form.

parameters.applies_to_fees: initial license and registration fees in B&P 7137(a)(3)
parameters.eligibility: veteran of U.S. Armed Forces incl. National Guard or Reserve, not dishonorably discharged
proof_options: state-issued driver's license or ID card with the word Veteran on its face
parameters.proof_timing: at time of board's request for initial license or registration fee

rules.applies_to: Veteran license applicants and HIS registrants
rules.verbatim_quote: The board shall grant a 50-percent reduction in the fees prescribed by this paragraph to an applicant who is a veteran of the United States Armed Forces, including the National Guard or Reserve components, and was not dishonorably discharged.
rules.notes: Applies to initial license/registration fees only (paragraph (3)), not application or renewal fees.

rules.title: CSLB license and HIS renewal fees
rules.plain_english: Renewal fees: individual owner active $450 (up to $563), inactive $300 (up to $375); partnership, corporation, LLC or joint venture active $700 (up to $875), inactive $500 (up to $625); HIS registration $200 (up to $250).
rules.applies_to: Licensees and HIS registrants renewing
rules.verbatim_quote: The renewal fee for an active license for an individual owner shall be four hundred fifty dollars ($450) and may be increased to not more than five hundred sixty-three dollars ($563).
rules.notes: Actual fee set by regulation within the cap; check current CSLB fee schedule. C-10 active renewals add $20 (7137(a)(6)(A)). 16 CCR 811 (PDF pages 451-452) currently sets these fees at the statutory base amounts.

verification.checked_against: 2026 CSLB Law Book (sources/lawbook.txt), PDF pages 375-376 (B&P 7137(a)(4)); 16 CCR 811 (PDF pages 451-452)
verification.correction: No error. All five renewal base/maximum pairs match 7137(a)(4)(A)-(E). Added a note that 16 CCR 811(d) (PDF pages 451-452) currently charges the base amounts.

rules.title: Late renewal: delinquency fee of 50% of renewal fee
rules.plain_english: If a license is renewed after it expires, a delinquency fee equal to 50% of the renewal fee is added.

parameters.formula: total = renewal_fee * 1.5 (plus any other applicable fees)

rules.applies_to: Licensees renewing after expiration
rules.verbatim_quote: The delinquency fee is an amount equal to 50 percent of the renewal fee, if the license is renewed after its expiration.
rules.notes: Formula derived from the text. Working on an expired license is also grounds for discipline (7117.5).

rules.title: C-10 contractors pay extra $20 at active renewal
rules.plain_english: C-10 (electrical) contractors pay an additional $20 with each active license renewal, used by CSLB to enforce Labor Code electrician certification rules.

parameters.assessed_with: renewal fee for an active license
parameters.purpose: enforce Labor Code electrician certification provisions

rules.applies_to: C-10 electrical contractors
rules.verbatim_quote: In addition to any other fees charged to C-10 contractors, the board shall charge a fee of twenty dollars ($20), to be assessed with the renewal fee for an active license, which shall be used by the board to enforce provisions of the Labor Code related to electrician certification.

rules.title: Licensee pays CSLB expert inspection costs if complaint ends in a final citation or LOA ($100 minimum; capped at CSLB cost)
rules.plain_english: If a public complaint required a professional or expert investigation or inspection and report (B&P 7019) and it resulted in a citation or letter of admonishment that became a final order, the licensee must pay a fee for each investigation or inspection and report. The fee may not be more than CSLB's cost of contracting for it, except that the minimum fee is $100; the statute lets that minimum be raised to no more than $1,000. The license will not be renewed until these fees are paid.

parameters.fee_cap: not more than board's cost of contracting for the investigation or inspection and report
parameters.max_usd_note: The statute sets no flat dollar maximum on the fee itself; grammatically "may be increased to not more than $1,000" modifies "the minimum fee". Many summaries read it as a $100-$1,000 range; treat $1,000 as a cap only if CSLB confirms.
parameters.per: each investigation or inspection and report
parameters.condition: resulted in a letter of admonishment or citation (B&P 7099, 7099.9) that became a final order of the registrar

rules.applies_to: Licensees subject to public complaints requiring expert inspection
rules.verbatim_quote: Fees shall be fixed in an amount not more than the board’s cost of contracting for the investigation or inspection and report, except that the minimum fee shall be one hundred dollars ($100) for each investigation or inspection and report and may be increased to not more than one thousand dollars ($1,000) for each investigation or inspection and report.
rules.notes: Ambiguous drafting: "except that the minimum fee shall be one hundred dollars ($100) ... and may be increased to not more than one thousand dollars ($1,000)". The subject of "may be increased" is the minimum fee; the general cap is the board's contracting cost. Do not tell a licensee their exposure is capped at $1,000 without confirming with CSLB.

verification.correction: Condition (final citation or LOA), per-report basis, cost-of-contracting cap, $100 minimum and renewal block confirmed. The rule stated max_usd = 1000 as a cap on the fee. In the text, "may be increased to not more than one thousand dollars ($1,000)" modifies "the minimum fee"; the fee itself is capped by the board's contracting cost, not by a flat $1,000. Replaced max_usd with statutory_minimum_usd 100, minimum_may_be_increased_to_not_more_than_usd 1000 and fee_cap (contract cost), set max_usd to null with an ambiguity note, and rewrote the title, plain_english and notes.

rules.title: Other CSLB fees: cash deposit, duplicate license, name change, bad check
rules.plain_english: Other CSLB fees: $100 service fee to deposit cash or a cashier's check instead of a bond; $25 for a duplicate license certificate; $100 (up to $125) to change the business name on a license; $25 for each dishonored check.

parameters.cash_deposit_basis: deposit under CCP 995.710(a)(1) in lieu of bond for Article 5 compliance

rules.applies_to: Licensees
rules.verbatim_quote: The fee to change the business name of a license as it is recorded under this chapter shall be one hundred dollars ($100) and may be increased to not more than one hundred twenty-five dollars ($125).
rules.notes: Business name changes must be filed so contracts match the licensed name (7117). 16 CCR 811(e)(1) (PDF page 452) currently sets the business name change fee at $100.

verification.checked_against: 2026 CSLB Law Book (sources/lawbook.txt), PDF pages 376-377 (B&P 7137(a)(6)(C)-(F)); 16 CCR 811(e) (PDF page 452)
verification.correction: No error. $100 deposit service fee, $25 duplicate certificate, $100 (max $125) name change and $25 dishonored check confirmed. Added a note that 16 CCR 811(e)(1) currently charges $100 for a name change.

rules.title: CSLB fees are earned and nonrefundable
rules.plain_english: Any fee paid for a CSLB service or application covered by B&P 7137 is earned when paid and will not be refunded, even if the application is withdrawn or denied.

parameters.covers: fees for services or applications under B&P 7137

rules.applies_to: Applicants and licensees
rules.verbatim_quote: a fee paid in connection with a service or application covered by Section 7137 shall accrue to the Contractors License Fund as an earned fee and shall not be refunded.
rules.notes: Unemployment Insurance Code 10501 (job training fee waiver) is referenced in the Appendix.

rules.title: Optional Construction Management Education contribution on fee form
rules.plain_english: When paying license fees, a contractor may make an optional contribution to the Construction Management Education Account. It is voluntary and in addition to required fees.

parameters.timing: at time of contractor license fee payment
parameters.account: Construction Management Education Account (Contractors License Fund)

rules.applies_to: Licensees paying fees
rules.verbatim_quote: The Contractors State License Board shall allow a contractor to make a contribution to the Construction Management Education Account at the time of the contractor license fee payment.
rules.notes: A fee calculator should not include this in required totals. Grant rules (7139.3-7139.5) concern universities and are omitted.

verification_summary.method: Every deadline, money_amount, threshold, penalty, required_notice and required_contract_clause rule (94) was read against the full section text in sources/lawbook.txt (PDF page N = form-feed page N). Every verbatim_quote was matched by machine against the normalized book text (line-end hyphens, running heads and margin tabs removed): all 151 match, apart from one hyphenation artifact ("Self-Insurance" split across a line) in a required_document rule. Titles, plain_english, parameters, effective dates and page references were compared with the statute text. Cross-references elsewhere in the book were checked: B&P 7071.6 (bond amount, PDF page 295), B&P 7099.8 (15-day citation contest deadline, "notwithstanding any other law"), 16 CCR 811 (current fee amounts, PDF pages 451-452) and 16 CCR 832 (classification names). Eight numeric rules in other categories were also checked (solar program repeal dates, informal citation conference, letter of admonishment retention, 7110.5 18-month rule, 7111 5-year records retention, 7118 penalty range, 7125.6 class codes, 7125.7 2027 audit).
